b2.en: Night fell quickly, but to my great amazement I found that the cottagers had a way of making light last longer by using candles, and I was delighted that sunset did not end the pleasure I felt in watching my human neighbours.
b2.ru: Ночь наступила быстро, но, к моему великому изумлению, я обнаружил, что обитатели дома умеют продлевать свет с помощью свечей, и был счастлив, что закат не положил конец удовольствию, с которым я наблюдал за своими соседями-людьми.

b2.en: In the evening the young girl and her companion were busy with various tasks that I did not understand, and the old man again picked up the instrument whose heavenly sounds had enchanted me in the morning.
b2.ru: Вечером девушка и её спутник занимались разными делами, которых я не понимал, а старик снова взял инструмент, чьи божественные звуки очаровали меня утром.

b2.en: As soon as he had finished, the young man began, not to play, but to make monotonous sounds that were like neither the harmony of the old man’s instrument nor the songs of the birds; I later found out that he was reading aloud, but at that time I knew nothing about words or letters.
b2.ru: Как только он закончил, юноша начал не играть, а произносить монотонные звуки, не похожие ни на гармонию стариковского инструмента, ни на пение птиц; позже я узнал, что он читал вслух, но тогда я ничего не знал ни о словах, ни о буквах.

b2.en: After spending a short time like this, the family put out their lights and went, as I guessed, to bed.
b2.ru: Проведя так недолгое время, семья погасила свет и отправилась, как я догадался, спать.

b1.en: It is very difficult for me to remember the first days of my life.
b1.ru: Мне очень трудно вспомнить первые дни моей жизни.

b1.en: Everything from that time seems confused and unclear.
b1.ru: Всё из того времени кажется спутанным и неясным.

b1.en: I had a lot of strange feelings all at once: I saw, felt, heard and smelt everything at the same time.
b1.ru: На меня сразу нахлынуло множество странных ощущений: я видел, чувствовал, слышал и чуял запахи одновременно.

b1.en: It took me a long time to learn the difference between my senses.
b1.ru: Мне понадобилось много времени, чтобы научиться различать свои чувства.

b1.en: I remember that slowly a stronger light began to hurt me, so I had to close my eyes.
b1.ru: Я помню, что постепенно более яркий свет стал причинять мне боль, и мне пришлось закрыть глаза.

b1.en: Then it became dark, and this worried me.
b1.ru: Потом стало темно, и это меня встревожило.

b1.en: But almost at once, I think, I opened my eyes, and the light came back.
b1.ru: Но почти сразу, думаю, я открыл глаза, и свет вернулся.

b1.en: I walked, and I believe I went down some stairs, but soon my feelings changed a lot.
b1.ru: Я пошёл и, кажется, спустился по лестнице, но скоро мои ощущения сильно изменились.

b1.en: Before, dark, solid things had been all around me, and I could not touch them or see through them.
b1.ru: Раньше вокруг меня были тёмные, плотные предметы, и я не мог ни потрогать их, ни увидеть сквозь них.

b1.en: But now I could walk wherever I wanted, and I could climb over or go around anything in my way.
b1.ru: Но теперь я мог ходить куда хотел и мог перелезть через любое препятствие или обойти его.

b1.en: The light became stronger and more painful, and the heat made me tired, so I looked for some shade.
b1.ru: Свет становился всё сильнее и мучительнее, а жара меня утомляла, и я стал искать тень.

b1.en: I found the forest near Ingolstadt.
b1.ru: Я нашёл лес под Ингольштадтом.

b1.en: There I lay down next to a stream and rested until I was very hungry and thirsty.
b1.ru: Там я лёг у ручья и отдыхал, пока не почувствовал сильный голод и жажду.

b1.en: This woke me up from my sleepy state, and I ate some berries from the trees and from the ground.
b1.ru: Это пробудило меня от сонного состояния, и я поел ягод с деревьев и с земли.

b1.en: I drank from the stream, and then I lay down and fell asleep.
b1.ru: Я напился из ручья, а потом лёг и уснул.

b1.en: When I woke up, it was dark.
b1.ru: Когда я проснулся, было темно.

b1.en: I was cold and a little frightened because I felt so alone.
b1.ru: Мне было холодно и немного страшно, потому что я чувствовал себя таким одиноким.

b1.en: Before I left your room, I had felt cold and put on some clothes, but they did not keep me warm in the wet night air.
b1.ru: Перед тем как уйти из твоей комнаты, я почувствовал холод и надел какую-то одежду, но она не согревала меня в сыром ночном воздухе.

b1.en: I was a poor, helpless, unhappy creature.
b1.ru: Я был бедным, беспомощным, несчастным существом.

b1.en: I knew nothing and understood nothing.
b1.ru: Я ничего не знал и ничего не понимал.

b1.en: I felt pain everywhere, so I sat down and cried.
b1.ru: Мне было больно везде, поэтому я сел и заплакал.

b1.en: Soon a soft light spread across the sky, and it made me feel good.
b1.ru: Вскоре по небу разлился мягкий свет, и мне стало приятно.

b1.en: I jumped up and saw something bright rise from behind the trees.
b1.ru: Я вскочил и увидел, как из-за деревьев поднимается что-то яркое.

b1.en: [The moon] I looked at it in wonder.
b1.ru: [Луна] Я смотрел на неё с удивлением.

b1.en: It moved slowly, but it lit my way, and I went to look for berries again.
b1.ru: Она двигалась медленно, но освещала мне дорогу, и я снова пошёл искать ягоды.

b1.en: I was still cold, but under a tree I found a big cloak.
b1.ru: Мне всё ещё было холодно, но под деревом я нашёл большой плащ.

b1.en: I put it round me and sat down on the ground.
b1.ru: Я закутался в него и сел на землю.

b1.en: I had no clear thoughts; everything was confused.
b1.ru: У меня не было ясных мыслей; всё было спутано.

b1.en: I felt light, hunger, thirst and darkness.
b1.ru: Я ощущал свет, голод, жажду и темноту.

b1.en: Many sounds rang in my ears, and there were smells all around me.
b1.ru: В ушах звенело множество звуков, и вокруг были разные запахи.

b1.en: The only thing I could see clearly was the bright moon, and I was happy to look at it.
b1.ru: Единственное, что я ясно видел, была яркая луна, и мне было радостно смотреть на неё.

b1.en: Several days and nights passed, and the moon became much smaller.
b1.ru: Прошло несколько дней и ночей, и луна стала намного меньше.

b1.en: Then I started to understand my different feelings.
b1.ru: Тогда я начал понимать свои разные ощущения.

b1.en: Slowly I began to see clearly the stream that gave me water and the trees that gave me shade.
b1.ru: Постепенно я стал ясно видеть ручей, дававший мне воду, и деревья, дававшие мне тень.

b1.en: I was very happy when I discovered that the pleasant sounds I often heard came from little animals with wings.
b1.ru: Я очень обрадовался, когда узнал, что приятные звуки, которые я часто слышал, издают маленькие крылатые существа.

b1.en: These animals often flew in front of my eyes and blocked the light.
b1.ru: Эти существа часто пролетали перед моими глазами и заслоняли свет.

b1.en: I also began to look more carefully at the shapes around me and at the edges of the bright sky above me.
b1.ru: Я также стал внимательнее рассматривать формы вокруг себя и края яркого неба надо мной.

b1.en: Sometimes I tried to copy the birds’ songs, but I couldn’t.
b1.ru: Иногда я пытался подражать пению птиц, но не мог.

b1.en: Sometimes I wanted to show my feelings in my own way, but the ugly, strange noises that came out of me frightened me, and I became silent again.
b1.ru: Иногда мне хотелось выразить свои чувства по-своему, но безобразные, странные звуки, которые вырывались из меня, пугали меня, и я снова замолкал.

b1.en: The moon disappeared and then came back, very thin, and I was still in the forest.
b1.ru: Луна исчезла, а потом вернулась, совсем тонкая, а я всё ещё был в лесу.

b1.en: By now my feelings were clear, and every day I learned new things.
b1.ru: К этому времени мои ощущения стали ясными, и каждый день я узнавал что-то новое.

b1.en: My eyes got used to the light, and I could see things in their real shapes.
b1.ru: Мои глаза привыкли к свету, и я мог видеть предметы в их настоящем виде.

b1.en: I could tell an insect from a plant, and later one plant from another.
b1.ru: Я мог отличить насекомое от растения, а позже и одно растение от другого.

b1.en: I found that the sparrow’s song was ugly, but the songs of the blackbird and the thrush were sweet and lovely.
b1.ru: Я понял, что воробей поёт некрасиво, а песни чёрного дрозда и певчего дрозда нежные и чудесные.

b1.en: One day, when I was very cold, I found a fire that some poor travellers had left.
b1.ru: Однажды, когда мне было очень холодно, я нашёл костёр, оставленный бедными бродягами.

b1.en: I was very happy to feel its warmth.
b1.ru: Я очень обрадовался его теплу.

b1.en: Full of joy, I put my hand into the hot coals, but I quickly pulled it out and cried with pain.
b1.ru: Радуясь, я сунул руку в горячие угли, но быстро выдернул её и закричал от боли.

b1.en: How strange, I thought, that the same thing can be so good and so bad!
b1.ru: Как странно, подумал я, что одно и то же может быть таким хорошим и таким плохим!

b1.en: I looked at the fire carefully and was glad to find that it was made of wood.
b1.ru: Я внимательно осмотрел костёр и с радостью понял, что он сделан из дерева.

b1.en: I quickly collected some branches, but they were wet and did not burn.
b1.ru: Я быстро собрал ветки, но они были мокрые и не горели.

b1.en: I was sad about this, and I sat quietly and watched the fire.
b1.ru: Меня это огорчило, и я тихо сидел и смотрел на огонь.

b1.en: The wet wood that I had put near the heat dried and started to burn.
b1.ru: Мокрые ветки, которые я положил рядом с огнём, высохли и начали гореть.

b1.en: I thought about this, and by touching the different branches, I understood why.
b1.ru: Я подумал об этом, потрогал разные ветки и понял почему.

b1.en: Then I collected a lot of wood so that I could dry it and always have enough fire.
b1.ru: Тогда я собрал много дров, чтобы высушить их и всегда иметь достаточно огня.

b1.en: When night came and I felt sleepy, I was very afraid that my fire would go out.
b1.ru: Когда наступила ночь и мне захотелось спать, я очень боялся, что мой огонь погаснет.

b1.en: I covered it carefully with dry wood and leaves and put wet branches on top.
b1.ru: Я осторожно укрыл его сухими ветками и листьями, а сверху положил мокрые ветки.

b1.en: Then I spread my cloak on the ground, lay down and fell asleep.
b1.ru: Потом я расстелил плащ на земле, лёг и уснул.

b1.en: It was morning when I woke up, and the first thing I did was look at the fire.
b1.ru: Когда я проснулся, было утро, и первым делом я посмотрел на огонь.

b1.en: I uncovered it, and a gentle wind soon made it burn again.
b1.ru: Я раскрыл его, и лёгкий ветер быстро снова раздул пламя.

b1.en: I noticed this too and made a fan from branches to wake up the fire when it was nearly out.
b1.ru: Я заметил и это и сделал из веток опахало, чтобы раздувать огонь, когда он почти гас.

b1.en: When night came again, I was pleased to find that the fire gave light as well as heat.
b1.ru: Когда снова наступила ночь, я с радостью обнаружил, что огонь даёт не только тепло, но и свет.

b1.en: It also helped me with my food.
b1.ru: Он помогал мне и с едой.

b1.en: The travellers had left some bits of meat, and the fire had cooked them; they tasted much better than the berries from the trees.
b1.ru: Путники оставили кусочки мяса, и огонь их поджарил; они были гораздо вкуснее ягод с деревьев.

b1.en: So I tried to cook my food in the same way on the hot coals.
b1.ru: Поэтому я стал так же готовить свою еду на горячих углях.

b1.en: I found that the fire spoiled the berries but made the nuts and roots much better.
b1.ru: Я понял, что огонь портит ягоды, но делает орехи и коренья гораздо вкуснее.

b1.en: But soon there was not much food, and I often spent the whole day looking for a few acorns to stop my hunger, but I found nothing.
b1.ru: Но скоро еды стало мало, и я часто целый день искал хоть несколько желудей, чтобы унять голод, но ничего не находил.

b1.en: So I decided to leave the place where I had lived and find another one where I could get what I needed more easily.
b1.ru: Поэтому я решил покинуть место, где жил, и найти другое, где легче будет добыть всё необходимое.

b1.en: I was very sorry to lose the fire, because I had found it by accident and did not know how to make it again.
b1.ru: Мне было очень жаль терять огонь, потому что я нашёл его случайно и не знал, как развести его снова.

b1.en: I thought about this problem for several hours, but in the end I had to give up.
b1.ru: Несколько часов я думал над этой задачей, но в конце концов мне пришлось сдаться.

b1.en: I wrapped my cloak around me and walked through the forest towards the setting sun.
b1.ru: Я закутался в плащ и пошёл через лес навстречу заходящему солнцу.

b1.en: I wandered for three days and at last came out into open country.
b1.ru: Я бродил три дня и наконец вышел на открытую местность.

b1.en: A lot of snow had fallen the night before, and the fields were all white.
b1.ru: Накануне ночью выпало много снега, и поля были совсем белыми.

b1.en: It looked sad and empty, and the cold, wet snow on the ground froze my feet.
b1.ru: Всё выглядело печальным и пустым, а холодный мокрый снег на земле морозил мне ноги.

b1.en: It was about seven in the morning, and I really wanted food and shelter.
b1.ru: Было около семи утра, и мне очень хотелось есть и найти укрытие.

b1.en: At last I saw a small hut on a hill; it was probably built for a shepherd.
b1.ru: Наконец я увидел на холме маленькую хижину; наверное, её построили для пастуха.

b1.en: I had never seen anything like it before, and I looked at it with great interest.
b1.ru: Я никогда раньше не видел ничего подобного и рассматривал её с большим интересом.

b1.en: The door was open, so I went in.
b1.ru: Дверь была открыта, и я вошёл.

b1.en: An old man was sitting by a fire and making his breakfast.
b1.ru: У огня сидел старик и готовил завтрак.

b1.en: He heard a noise and turned round, and when he saw me, he screamed.
b1.ru: Он услышал шум и обернулся, а увидев меня, закричал.

b1.en: He ran out of the hut and across the fields, faster than I thought his weak old body could go.
b1.ru: Он выбежал из хижины и побежал по полю быстрее, чем, казалось бы, могло его слабое старое тело.

b1.en: He looked different from anything I had seen before, and his running away surprised me a little.
b1.ru: Он выглядел не так, как всё, что я видел раньше, и его бегство меня немного удивило.

b1.en: But I loved the hut.
b1.ru: Но хижина мне очень понравилась.

b1.en: Snow and rain could not get in, and the floor was dry.
b1.ru: Снег и дождь не проникали внутрь, и пол был сухим.

b1.en: To me it seemed as wonderful as Pandæmonium seemed to the devils of hell after their suffering in the lake of fire.
b1.ru: Она казалась мне такой же чудесной, каким казался Пандемоний бесам ада после их мучений в огненном озере.

b1.en: I hungrily ate what was left of the shepherd’s breakfast: bread, cheese, milk and wine.
b1.ru: Я жадно съел остатки пастушьего завтрака: хлеб, сыр, молоко и вино.

b1.en: But I didn’t like the wine.
b1.ru: Но вино мне не понравилось.

b1.en: Then, very tired, I lay down on some straw and fell asleep.
b1.ru: Потом, очень усталый, я лёг на солому и уснул.

b1.en: When I woke up, it was midday.
b1.ru: Когда я проснулся, был полдень.

b1.en: The warm sun was shining brightly on the white snow, and I decided to continue my journey.
b1.ru: Тёплое солнце ярко сияло на белом снегу, и я решил продолжить путь.

b1.en: I put the rest of the breakfast into a bag that I found, and I walked across the fields for several hours.
b1.ru: Я положил остатки завтрака в найденную сумку и несколько часов шёл полями.

b1.en: At sunset I came to a village.
b1.ru: На закате я пришёл в деревню.

b1.en: It seemed like a miracle!
b1.ru: Она показалась мне чудом!

b1.en: I admired the huts, the nicer cottages and the big, beautiful houses.
b1.ru: Я любовался хижинами, более красивыми домиками и большими прекрасными домами.

b1.en: The vegetables in the gardens and the milk and cheese in the windows of some cottages made me hungry.
b1.ru: Овощи в огородах, молоко и сыр в окнах некоторых домов вызвали у меня голод.

b1.en: I went into one of the best houses, but as soon as I stepped inside, the children screamed and one of the women fainted.
b1.ru: Я вошёл в один из лучших домов, но как только я переступил порог, дети закричали, а одна женщина упала в обморок.

b1.en: The whole village woke up.
b1.ru: Вся деревня поднялась.

b1.en: Some people ran away, and some attacked me.
b1.ru: Одни люди убежали, другие напали на меня.

b1.en: They threw stones and other things at me and hurt me badly, and at last I escaped into the fields.
b1.ru: Они бросали в меня камни и другие предметы и сильно меня избили, и наконец я убежал в поле.

b1.en: I was afraid, and I hid in a low, empty shed; it looked very poor after the palaces I had seen in the village.
b1.ru: Мне было страшно, и я спрятался в низком пустом сарае; он выглядел очень бедным после дворцов, которые я видел в деревне.

b1.en: This shed was joined to a nice, clean cottage, but after my painful experience, I didn’t dare to go in.
b1.ru: Этот сарай примыкал к милому чистому домику, но после такого горького опыта я не посмел туда войти.

b1.en: My shelter was made of wood, but it was so low that I could hardly sit up straight in it.
b1.ru: Моё укрытие было деревянным, но таким низким, что я едва мог сидеть в нём прямо.

b1.en: The floor was just earth, but it was dry, and although the wind came in through many holes, it was a good place to hide from the snow and rain.
b1.ru: Пол был просто земляной, но сухой, и хотя ветер задувал через множество щелей, это было хорошее место, чтобы укрыться от снега и дождя.

b1.en: So I lay down there, happy to have a shelter, even a poor one, from the bad weather and, even more, from cruel people.
b1.ru: И я лёг там, радуясь, что у меня есть укрытие, пусть и бедное, от плохой погоды и, ещё больше, от жестоких людей.

b1.en: In the morning I crawled out of my little hole to look at the cottage next to it and to see if I could stay where I was.
b1.ru: Утром я выполз из своей норы, чтобы посмотреть на соседний дом и понять, могу ли я остаться там, где был.

b1.en: My shed stood against the back wall of the cottage.
b1.ru: Мой сарай стоял у задней стены дома.

b1.en: On its other sides there was a pigsty and a pool of clear water.
b1.ru: С других сторон были свинарник и пруд с чистой водой.

b1.en: One side was open, and I had crawled in that way.
b1.ru: Одна сторона была открыта, и через неё я заполз внутрь.

b1.en: Now I covered every hole with stones and wood so that nobody could see me, but I could still move them when I wanted to go out.
b1.ru: Теперь я закрыл каждую щель камнями и деревом, чтобы никто меня не видел, но так, чтобы я мог отодвинуть их, когда захочу выйти.

b1.en: All my light came through the pigsty, and that was enough for me.
b1.ru: Весь свет проникал ко мне через свинарник, и мне этого хватало.

b1.en: I made my home ready and put clean straw on the floor.
b1.ru: Я обустроил своё жилище и постелил на пол чистую солому.

b1.en: Then I hid, because I saw a man far away.
b1.ru: Потом я спрятался, потому что увидел вдали человека.

b1.en: I remembered very well how people had treated me the night before, and I didn’t want to be in his power.
b1.ru: Я слишком хорошо помнил, как люди обошлись со мной накануне, и не хотел оказаться в его власти.

b1.en: But first I had stolen a loaf of rough bread for the day, and I had taken a cup, so that I could drink the clean water that ran past my shelter more easily than from my hand.
b1.ru: Но сначала я украл буханку грубого хлеба на день и взял чашку, чтобы пить чистую воду, которая текла мимо моего укрытия, удобнее, чем из ладони.

b1.en: The floor was a little higher than the ground, so it stayed dry, and it was quite warm because it was near the cottage chimney.
b1.ru: Пол был немного выше земли, поэтому оставался сухим, и там было довольно тепло, потому что рядом была труба дома.

b1.en: Now I had what I needed, and I decided to live in this shed until something changed my plans.
b1.ru: Теперь у меня было всё необходимое, и я решил жить в этом сарае, пока что-нибудь не изменит мои планы.

b1.en: It was really a paradise compared with the cold forest where I had lived before, with its wet branches and damp ground.
b1.ru: Это был настоящий рай по сравнению с холодным лесом, где я жил раньше, с его мокрыми ветками и сырой землёй.

b1.en: I enjoyed my breakfast and was going to move a board to get some water when I heard footsteps.
b1.ru: Я с удовольствием позавтракал и собирался отодвинуть доску, чтобы набрать воды, как вдруг услышал шаги.

b1.en: I looked through a small hole and saw a young woman with a bucket on her head walking past my shed.
b1.ru: Я посмотрел в маленькую щель и увидел молодую женщину с ведром на голове, проходившую мимо моего сарая.

b1.en: The girl was young and gentle, not like the country people and farm servants I met later.
b1.ru: Девушка была юной и кроткой, не похожей на деревенских жителей и батраков, которых я встречал позже.

b1.en: But her clothes were poor: a rough blue skirt and a simple jacket.
b1.ru: Но одежда у неё была бедная: грубая синяя юбка и простая кофта.

b1.en: Her fair hair was in a plait, with no decoration.
b1.ru: Её светлые волосы были заплетены в косу без всяких украшений.

b1.en: She looked patient but sad.
b1.ru: Она выглядела терпеливой, но печальной.

b1.en: She went away, and about fifteen minutes later she came back with the bucket, which was now partly full of milk.
b1.ru: Она ушла, а минут через пятнадцать вернулась с ведром, теперь наполовину полным молока.

b1.en: The bucket seemed heavy for her.
b1.ru: Ведро казалось для неё тяжёлым.

b1.en: Then a young man met her, and his face looked even sadder than hers.
b1.ru: Тут её встретил юноша, и его лицо было ещё печальнее, чем у неё.

b1.en: He said a few words sadly, took the bucket from her head and carried it to the cottage himself.
b1.ru: Он печально сказал несколько слов, снял ведро с её головы и сам отнёс его в дом.

b1.en: She followed him, and they went inside.
b1.ru: Она пошла за ним, и они вошли внутрь.

b1.en: Soon I saw the young man again; he was walking across the field behind the cottage with some tools in his hand.
b1.ru: Вскоре я снова увидел юношу: он шёл через поле за домом с инструментами в руках.

b1.en: The girl was busy too, sometimes in the house and sometimes in the yard.
b1.ru: Девушка тоже была занята — то в доме, то во дворе.

b1.en: When I looked around my shed, I found that there had once been a window of the cottage there, but it was now covered with wood.
b1.ru: Осмотрев свой сарай, я обнаружил, что когда-то там было окно дома, но теперь оно было заколочено досками.

b1.en: In the wood there was a very small crack, and I could just see through it.
b1.ru: В досках была очень маленькая щель, и сквозь неё едва можно было что-то увидеть.

b1.en: Through this crack I could see a small room.
b1.ru: Сквозь эту щель я видел маленькую комнату.

b1.en: It was white and clean, but there was almost no furniture.
b1.ru: Она была белой и чистой, но мебели почти не было.

b1.en: In one corner, near a small fire, an old man was sitting with his head in his hands, and he looked very unhappy.
b1.ru: В углу, у маленького огня, сидел старик, обхватив голову руками, и выглядел очень несчастным.

b1.en: The young girl was cleaning the cottage.
b1.ru: Девушка прибиралась в доме.

b1.en: Then she took some work out of a drawer and sat down next to the old man.
b1.ru: Потом она достала из ящика какое-то рукоделие и села рядом со стариком.

b1.en: He picked up a musical instrument and began to play; the music was sweeter than the song of the thrush or the nightingale.
b1.ru: Он взял музыкальный инструмент и начал играть; музыка была нежнее пения дрозда или соловья.

b1.en: It was a beautiful picture, even for me, a poor creature who had never seen anything beautiful before.
b1.ru: Это была прекрасная картина даже для меня, бедного существа, никогда прежде не видевшего ничего красивого.

b1.en: I respected the old man with his silver hair and kind face, and I loved the girl for her gentle ways.
b1.ru: Я почитал старика с его серебряными волосами и добрым лицом и полюбил девушку за её кротость.

b1.en: He played a sweet, sad song, and I saw that it made his lovely companion cry.
b1.ru: Он играл нежную, грустную мелодию, и я увидел, что его милая спутница заплакала.

b1.en: The old man did not notice until she began to sob loudly.
b1.ru: Старик не замечал этого, пока она не начала громко всхлипывать.

b1.en: Then he said a few words, and the beautiful girl stopped her work and knelt at his feet.
b1.ru: Тогда он сказал несколько слов, и прекрасная девушка оставила работу и опустилась на колени у его ног.

b1.en: He lifted her up and smiled at her with such kindness and love that I had very strange and strong feelings.
b1.ru: Он поднял её и улыбнулся ей с такой добротой и любовью, что меня охватили очень странные и сильные чувства.

b1.en: They were a mixture of pain and pleasure, and I had never felt anything like them from hunger or cold, or from warmth or food.
b1.ru: Это была смесь боли и радости, и ничего подобного я никогда не испытывал ни от голода или холода, ни от тепла или еды.

b1.en: I moved away from the window because I could not bear these emotions.
b1.ru: Я отошёл от окна, потому что не мог вынести этих переживаний.

b1.en: Soon after this the young man came back, carrying some wood on his shoulders.
b1.ru: Вскоре после этого вернулся юноша, неся на плечах дрова.

b1.en: The girl met him at the door and helped him with his heavy load.
b1.ru: Девушка встретила его у двери и помогла ему с тяжёлой ношей.

b1.en: She took some of the wood into the cottage and put it on the fire.
b1.ru: Она внесла часть дров в дом и положила их в огонь.

b1.en: Then she and the young man went into a corner, and he showed her a large loaf of bread and a piece of cheese.
b1.ru: Потом они с юношей отошли в угол, и он показал ей большую буханку хлеба и кусок сыра.

b1.en: She seemed happy and went into the garden to get some roots and plants.
b1.ru: Она, казалось, обрадовалась и пошла в огород за кореньями и травами.

b1.en: She put them in water and then on the fire.
b1.ru: Она положила их в воду, а затем на огонь.

b1.en: After that she continued her work, and the young man went into the garden and was busy digging and pulling up roots.
b1.ru: После этого она продолжила работу, а юноша вышел в огород и усердно копал и выдёргивал коренья.

b1.en: After about an hour the young woman joined him, and they went into the cottage together.
b1.ru: Примерно через час девушка присоединилась к нему, и они вместе вошли в дом.

b1.en: All this time the old man had been thinking quietly, but when the young people came in, he looked happier, and they sat down to eat.
b1.ru: Всё это время старик тихо размышлял, но когда молодые люди вошли, он повеселел, и они сели есть.

b1.en: They finished the meal quickly.
b1.ru: Они быстро закончили трапезу.

b1.en: The young woman started cleaning the cottage again, and the old man walked in the sun in front of the cottage for a few minutes, holding the young man’s arm.
b1.ru: Девушка снова принялась убирать в доме, а старик несколько минут гулял на солнце перед домом, держась за руку юноши.

b1.en: Nothing could be more beautiful than the difference between these two wonderful people.
b1.ru: Ничто не могло быть прекраснее, чем различие между этими двумя чудесными людьми.

b1.en: One was old, with silver hair and a face full of kindness and love.
b1.ru: Один был стар, с серебряными волосами и лицом, полным доброты и любви.

b1.en: The younger one was slim and graceful, with a very handsome face, but his eyes and the way he stood showed deep sadness.
b1.ru: Младший был строен и изящен, с очень красивым лицом, но его глаза и то, как он стоял, выдавали глубокую печаль.

b1.en: The old man went back into the cottage, and the young man took some different tools and walked across the fields.
b1.ru: Старик вернулся в дом, а юноша взял другие инструменты и пошёл через поле.

b1.en: Night came quickly, but to my great surprise the family had a way to make light: they used candles.
b1.ru: Ночь наступила быстро, но, к моему большому удивлению, у семьи был способ получать свет: они зажигали свечи.

b1.en: I was very glad, because the sunset did not stop my pleasure in watching my human neighbours.
b1.ru: Я очень обрадовался, потому что закат не лишил меня удовольствия наблюдать за своими соседями-людьми.

b1.en: In the evening the girl and the young man did different things that I did not understand, and the old man played again the instrument that had made such beautiful music in the morning.
b1.ru: Вечером девушка и юноша занимались разными делами, которых я не понимал, а старик снова играл на инструменте, который утром издавал такую прекрасную музыку.

b1.en: When he finished, the young man began to make sounds, but he did not play.
b1.ru: Когда он закончил, юноша начал издавать звуки, но не играл.

b1.en: The sounds were all the same, and they were not like the old man’s music or the songs of the birds.
b1.ru: Звуки были однообразными и не походили ни на музыку старика, ни на пение птиц.

b1.en: Later I learned that he was reading aloud, but at that time I knew nothing about words or letters.
b1.ru: Позже я узнал, что он читал вслух, но тогда я ничего не знал ни о словах, ни о буквах.

b1.en: After a short time the family put out their lights and went, I guessed, to sleep.
b1.ru: Через некоторое время семья погасила свет и пошла, как я догадался, спать.

a2.en: It is hard for me to remember the first days of my life.
a2.ru: Мне трудно вспомнить первые дни моей жизни.

a2.en: Everything from that time is not clear.
a2.ru: Всё из того времени неясно.

a2.en: I saw, heard, felt and smelt many things at the same time.
a2.ru: Я видел, слышал, чувствовал и чуял запахи одновременно.

a2.en: For a long time I didn’t know the difference between them.
a2.ru: Долгое время я не понимал разницы между ними.

a2.en: Then a strong light hurt my eyes, so I closed them.
a2.ru: Потом яркий свет стал резать мне глаза, и я их закрыл.

a2.en: Everything went dark, and I didn’t like it, so I opened my eyes again.
a2.ru: Всё потемнело, мне это не понравилось, и я снова открыл глаза.

a2.en: I walked, and I think I went down some stairs.
a2.ru: Я пошёл и, кажется, спустился по лестнице.

a2.en: Soon everything felt different.
a2.ru: Скоро всё стало ощущаться по-другому.

a2.en: Before, there were dark things all around me.
a2.ru: Раньше вокруг меня были тёмные предметы.

a2.en: Now I could walk anywhere, and nothing stopped me.
a2.ru: Теперь я мог идти куда угодно, и ничто меня не останавливало.

a2.en: The light was too strong and the day was hot, so I looked for some shade.
a2.ru: Свет был слишком ярким, а день жарким, поэтому я искал тень.

a2.en: I came to the forest near Ingolstadt.
a2.ru: Я пришёл в лес под Ингольштадтом.

a2.en: I lay down next to a small river and rested.
a2.ru: Я лёг у маленькой речки и отдохнул.

a2.en: Then I was hungry and thirsty, so I ate some berries from the trees and the ground.
a2.ru: Потом мне захотелось есть и пить, и я поел ягод с деревьев и с земли.

a2.en: I drank some water from the river and went to sleep.
a2.ru: Я попил воды из речки и уснул.

a2.en: When I woke up, it was dark.
a2.ru: Когда я проснулся, было темно.

a2.en: I was cold, and I was a little afraid because I was alone.
a2.ru: Мне было холодно и немного страшно, потому что я был один.

a2.en: Before I left your room, I put on some clothes, but they were not warm enough for the night.
a2.ru: Перед тем как уйти из твоей комнаты, я надел какую-то одежду, но она была недостаточно тёплой для ночи.

a2.en: I was a poor, weak, unhappy creature.
a2.ru: Я был бедным, слабым, несчастным существом.

a2.en: I didn’t know anything.
a2.ru: Я ничего не знал.

a2.en: Everything hurt, so I sat down and cried.
a2.ru: Мне было больно, поэтому я сел и заплакал.

a2.en: Soon a soft light came into the sky, and I liked it.
a2.ru: Скоро на небе появился мягкий свет, и он мне понравился.

a2.en: I stood up and saw something bright over the trees.
a2.ru: Я встал и увидел над деревьями что-то яркое.

a2.en: [The moon] I looked at it for a long time.
a2.ru: [Луна] Я долго смотрел на неё.

a2.en: It gave me light, and I went to find more berries.
a2.ru: Она давала мне свет, и я пошёл искать ещё ягод.

a2.en: Under a tree I found a big coat.
a2.ru: Под деревом я нашёл большое пальто.

a2.en: I put it on and sat on the ground.
a2.ru: Я надел его и сел на землю.

a2.en: I couldn’t think clearly.
a2.ru: Я не мог ясно думать.

a2.en: There were many sounds and smells around me.
a2.ru: Вокруг было много звуков и запахов.

a2.en: I was happy to look at the bright moon.
a2.ru: Мне было радостно смотреть на яркую луну.

a2.en: Many days and nights passed, and the moon got smaller.
a2.ru: Прошло много дней и ночей, и луна стала меньше.

a2.en: Slowly I began to understand my feelings.
a2.ru: Постепенно я начал понимать свои ощущения.

a2.en: I could see the river that gave me water and the trees that gave me shade.
a2.ru: Я видел речку, которая давала мне воду, и деревья, которые давали мне тень.

a2.en: I often heard beautiful sounds.
a2.ru: Я часто слышал красивые звуки.

a2.en: One day I learned that they came from small birds, and I was very happy.
a2.ru: Однажды я понял, что их издают маленькие птицы, и очень обрадовался.

a2.en: I tried to sing like the birds, but I couldn’t.
a2.ru: Я пытался петь, как птицы, но не мог.

a2.en: When I tried to speak, only ugly noises came out of my mouth.
a2.ru: Когда я пытался говорить, изо рта выходили только некрасивые звуки.

a2.en: They frightened me, so I stopped.
a2.ru: Они меня пугали, и я замолкал.

a2.en: The moon went away and came back again, and I was still in the forest.
a2.ru: Луна исчезла и появилась снова, а я всё ещё был в лесу.

a2.en: Now I understood my feelings better, and every day I learned something new.
a2.ru: Теперь я лучше понимал свои ощущения и каждый день узнавал что-то новое.

a2.en: My eyes got used to the light.
a2.ru: Мои глаза привыкли к свету.

a2.en: I could see the difference between an insect and a plant, and between different plants.
a2.ru: Я видел разницу между насекомым и растением и между разными растениями.

a2.en: I learned that some birds sing badly, but other birds sing very sweetly.
a2.ru: Я узнал, что некоторые птицы поют плохо, а другие — очень нежно.

a2.en: One cold day I found a fire.
a2.ru: Однажды в холодный день я нашёл костёр.

a2.en: Some poor travellers left it there.
a2.ru: Его оставили какие-то бедные путники.

a2.en: It was warm, and I was very happy.
a2.ru: Он был тёплым, и я очень обрадовался.

a2.en: I put my hand into the fire, but it hurt, and I shouted and pulled it out.
a2.ru: Я сунул руку в огонь, но мне стало больно, я закричал и выдернул её.

a2.en: How strange, I thought: the same thing can be good and bad!
a2.ru: Как странно, подумал я: одна и та же вещь может быть и хорошей, и плохой!

a2.en: I looked at the fire and saw that it was made of wood.
a2.ru: Я посмотрел на костёр и увидел, что он из дерева.

a2.en: I brought some branches, but they were wet and didn’t burn.
a2.ru: Я принёс веток, но они были мокрые и не горели.

a2.en: I was sad, and I sat and watched the fire.
a2.ru: Мне стало грустно, и я сидел и смотрел на огонь.

a2.en: After some time the wet wood near the fire got dry and began to burn.
a2.ru: Через некоторое время мокрые ветки у огня высохли и загорелись.

a2.en: Now I understood!
a2.ru: Теперь я понял!

a2.en: I collected a lot of wood and dried it, so I always had a fire.
a2.ru: Я собрал много дров и высушил их, чтобы у меня всегда был огонь.

a2.en: At night I was afraid that the fire was going to go out.
a2.ru: Ночью я боялся, что огонь погаснет.

a2.en: So I covered it with dry wood, leaves and wet branches.
a2.ru: Поэтому я укрыл его сухими ветками, листьями и мокрыми ветками.

a2.en: Then I lay down on my coat and went to sleep.
a2.ru: Потом я лёг на своё пальто и уснул.

a2.en: In the morning I went to the fire first.
a2.ru: Утром я первым делом пошёл к огню.

a2.en: The wind helped it to burn again.
a2.ru: Ветер помог ему снова разгореться.

a2.en: So I made a fan from branches and used it when the fire was nearly out.
a2.ru: Поэтому я сделал из веток опахало и пользовался им, когда огонь почти гас.

a2.en: At night the fire gave me light, too.
a2.ru: Ночью огонь давал мне ещё и свет.

a2.en: I also found some meat that the travellers left.
a2.ru: Я также нашёл мясо, которое оставили путники.

a2.en: The fire cooked it, and it was much nicer than berries.
a2.ru: Огонь поджарил его, и оно было гораздо вкуснее ягод.

a2.en: So I started to cook my food on the fire.
a2.ru: Тогда я начал готовить еду на огне.

a2.en: Berries were bad when I cooked them, but nuts and roots were better.
a2.ru: Жареные ягоды были невкусными, а орехи и коренья — лучше.

a2.en: But soon there wasn’t much food.
a2.ru: Но скоро еды стало мало.

a2.en: I often looked for food all day, but I found nothing.
a2.ru: Я часто искал еду весь день, но ничего не находил.

a2.en: So I decided to leave and find a better place.
a2.ru: Поэтому я решил уйти и найти место получше.

a2.en: I was very sad because I couldn’t take the fire with me, and I didn’t know how to make a new one.
a2.ru: Мне было очень грустно, потому что я не мог взять огонь с собой и не знал, как развести новый.

a2.en: I thought about it for hours, but I found no answer.
a2.ru: Я думал об этом несколько часов, но не нашёл ответа.

a2.en: I put on my coat and walked through the forest towards the evening sun.
a2.ru: Я надел пальто и пошёл через лес навстречу вечернему солнцу.

a2.en: After three days I came out of the forest.
a2.ru: Через три дня я вышел из леса.

a2.en: There was a lot of snow, and the fields were white.
a2.ru: Было много снега, и поля были белыми.

a2.en: It was a sad place, and my feet were very cold.
a2.ru: Это было печальное место, и мои ноги очень мёрзли.

a2.en: It was seven in the morning, and I wanted food and a warm place.
a2.ru: Было семь утра, и мне хотелось еды и тёплого места.

a2.en: Then I saw a small hut on a hill.
a2.ru: Потом я увидел маленькую хижину на холме.

a2.en: I was interested because I never saw a house before.
a2.ru: Мне стало интересно, потому что я никогда раньше не видел дома.

a2.en: The door was open, so I went in.
a2.ru: Дверь была открыта, и я вошёл.

a2.en: An old man was sitting by the fire and cooking his breakfast.
a2.ru: У огня сидел старик и готовил себе завтрак.

a2.en: He turned round and saw me.
a2.ru: Он обернулся и увидел меня.

a2.en: He screamed and ran out of the hut and across the fields very fast.
a2.ru: Он закричал, выбежал из хижины и очень быстро побежал по полю.

a2.en: I was surprised.
a2.ru: Я удивился.

a2.en: But I loved the hut.
a2.ru: Но хижина мне очень понравилась.

a2.en: It was dry inside, and the snow and rain couldn’t come in.
a2.ru: Внутри было сухо, и снег и дождь не попадали внутрь.

a2.en: For me it was a wonderful place, like a palace.
a2.ru: Для меня это было чудесное место, как дворец.

a2.en: I quickly ate the old man’s breakfast: bread, cheese, milk and wine.
a2.ru: Я быстро съел завтрак старика: хлеб, сыр, молоко и вино.

a2.en: I didn’t like the wine.
a2.ru: Вино мне не понравилось.

a2.en: Then I was very tired, so I lay down and slept.
a2.ru: Потом я очень устал, лёг и уснул.

a2.en: I woke up at midday.
a2.ru: Я проснулся в полдень.

a2.en: The sun was warm, so I decided to walk on.
a2.ru: Солнце было тёплым, и я решил идти дальше.

a2.en: I put the rest of the food in a bag and walked for many hours.
a2.ru: Я положил остатки еды в сумку и шёл много часов.

a2.en: In the evening I came to a village.
a2.ru: Вечером я пришёл в деревню.

a2.en: It was wonderful!
a2.ru: Это было чудесно!

a2.en: There were small houses and big beautiful houses.
a2.ru: Там были маленькие домики и большие красивые дома.

a2.en: I saw vegetables in the gardens and milk and cheese in the windows, and I was hungry.
a2.ru: Я видел овощи в огородах, молоко и сыр в окнах, и мне захотелось есть.

a2.en: I went into one of the houses, but the children screamed and a woman fell down.
a2.ru: Я вошёл в один из домов, но дети закричали, а одна женщина упала в обморок.

a2.en: All the people in the village came out.
a2.ru: Все жители деревни выбежали на улицу.

a2.en: Some ran away, and some threw stones at me.
a2.ru: Одни убежали, а другие бросали в меня камни.

a2.en: They hurt me, and I ran away into the fields.
a2.ru: Они меня поранили, и я убежал в поле.

a2.en: I was afraid, and I hid in a small, empty shed.
a2.ru: Мне было страшно, и я спрятался в маленьком пустом сарае.

a2.en: It was next to a nice little house, but I didn’t go into the house.
a2.ru: Он стоял рядом с милым домиком, но в дом я не пошёл.

a2.en: The shed was very low, and I couldn’t sit up straight.
a2.ru: Сарай был очень низким, и я не мог сидеть прямо.

a2.en: The wind came in, but it was dry, and the snow and rain didn’t come in.
a2.ru: Ветер задувал внутрь, но там было сухо, и снег и дождь не попадали внутрь.

a2.en: I lay down there.
a2.ru: Я лёг там.

a2.en: I was happy because I was safe from the cold weather and from cruel people.
a2.ru: Я был рад, потому что спрятался от холодной погоды и от жестоких людей.

a2.en: In the morning I went out quietly and looked at the house.
a2.ru: Утром я тихо вышел и осмотрел дом.

a2.en: My shed was at the back of the house.
a2.ru: Мой сарай был у задней стены дома.

a2.en: Next to it there were some pigs and a small lake.
a2.ru: Рядом были свиньи и маленький пруд.

a2.en: I closed all the holes in the shed with stones and wood, so nobody could see me.
a2.ru: Я закрыл все дыры в сарае камнями и деревом, чтобы никто меня не видел.

a2.en: A little light came in, and that was enough for me.
a2.ru: Внутрь проникало немного света, и мне этого хватало.

a2.en: I put clean straw on the floor.
a2.ru: Я постелил на пол чистую солому.

a2.en: Then I saw a man and hid, because I remembered the people in the village.
a2.ru: Потом я увидел человека и спрятался, потому что помнил людей в деревне.

a2.en: But first I took some bread and a cup.
a2.ru: Но сначала я взял хлеба и чашку.

a2.en: Now I could drink water from the river next to my shed.
a2.ru: Теперь я мог пить воду из речки рядом с сараем.

a2.en: The floor was dry, and it was quite warm because the house’s chimney was near.
a2.ru: Пол был сухим, и было довольно тепло, потому что рядом была труба дома.

a2.en: I decided to stay in the shed.
a2.ru: Я решил остаться в сарае.

a2.en: It was much better than the cold, wet forest.
a2.ru: Там было гораздо лучше, чем в холодном мокром лесу.

a2.en: I had my breakfast, and then I heard someone.
a2.ru: Я позавтракал, а потом услышал чьи-то шаги.

a2.en: I looked through a small hole and saw a young girl with a bucket on her head.
a2.ru: Я посмотрел в маленькую дырочку и увидел девушку с ведром на голове.

a2.en: The girl was young and kind.
a2.ru: Девушка была юной и доброй.

a2.en: She wore poor clothes, and her hair was long and fair.
a2.ru: Она была бедно одета, а волосы у неё были длинные и светлые.

a2.en: She looked sad.
a2.ru: Она выглядела грустной.

a2.en: She went away and came back with some milk in the bucket.
a2.ru: Она ушла и вернулась с молоком в ведре.

a2.en: The bucket was heavy.
a2.ru: Ведро было тяжёлым.

a2.en: A young man came to meet her.
a2.ru: Навстречу ей вышел юноша.

a2.en: He looked even sadder than her.
a2.ru: Он выглядел ещё печальнее, чем она.

a2.en: He took the bucket and carried it into the house, and she followed him.
a2.ru: Он взял ведро и понёс его в дом, а она пошла за ним.

a2.en: Later the young man went across the field with some tools.
a2.ru: Позже юноша пошёл через поле с инструментами.

a2.en: The girl worked in the house and in the garden.
a2.ru: Девушка работала в доме и во дворе.

a2.en: In my shed I found an old window of the house.
a2.ru: В своём сарае я нашёл старое окно дома.

a2.en: It was covered with wood, but there was a very small hole in it.
a2.ru: Оно было заколочено досками, но в них была очень маленькая дырочка.

a2.en: Through the hole I could see a small, clean room with very little furniture.
a2.ru: Через дырочку я видел маленькую чистую комнату почти без мебели.

a2.en: An old man was sitting near the fire with his head in his hands.
a2.ru: У огня сидел старик, обхватив голову руками.

a2.en: He looked very sad.
a2.ru: Он выглядел очень грустным.

a2.en: The girl cleaned the room.
a2.ru: Девушка прибралась в комнате.

a2.en: Then she sat down next to the old man and worked with her hands.
a2.ru: Потом она села рядом со стариком и занялась рукоделием.

a2.en: The old man began to play music.
a2.ru: Старик начал играть музыку.

a2.en: It was more beautiful than the songs of the birds.
a2.ru: Она была прекраснее пения птиц.

a2.en: I never saw anything so beautiful before.
a2.ru: Я никогда раньше не видел ничего столь прекрасного.

a2.en: I liked the kind old man with his white hair, and I loved the gentle girl.
a2.ru: Мне понравился добрый старик с седыми волосами, и я полюбил кроткую девушку.

a2.en: The music was sad, and the girl began to cry.
a2.ru: Музыка была печальной, и девушка заплакала.

a2.en: The old man didn’t see her tears, but then he heard her.
a2.ru: Старик не видел её слёз, но потом услышал её.

a2.en: He said something, and she went to him and knelt down.
a2.ru: Он что-то сказал, и она подошла к нему и опустилась на колени.

a2.en: He helped her up and smiled at her kindly.
a2.ru: Он помог ей подняться и ласково ей улыбнулся.

a2.en: I felt something new and very strong, pain and happiness together.
a2.ru: Я почувствовал что-то новое и очень сильное — боль и счастье вместе.

a2.en: I moved away from the hole because it was too much for me.
a2.ru: Я отошёл от дырочки, потому что это было для меня слишком.

a2.en: Then the young man came back with some wood.
a2.ru: Потом вернулся юноша с дровами.

a2.en: The girl helped him and put some wood on the fire.
a2.ru: Девушка помогла ему и подложила дров в огонь.

a2.en: He showed her some bread and cheese, and she was happy.
a2.ru: Он показал ей хлеб и сыр, и она обрадовалась.

a2.en: She brought some vegetables from the garden and cooked them.
a2.ru: Она принесла из огорода овощи и сварила их.

a2.en: The young man worked in the garden.
a2.ru: Юноша работал в огороде.

a2.en: After an hour the girl came to him, and they went into the house together.
a2.ru: Через час девушка пришла к нему, и они вместе вошли в дом.

a2.en: The old man was quiet, but when the young people came in, he looked happier.
a2.ru: Старик был молчалив, но когда молодые люди вошли, он повеселел.

a2.en: They ate their meal quickly.
a2.ru: Они быстро поели.

a2.en: The girl cleaned the house again.
a2.ru: Девушка снова прибралась в доме.

a2.en: The old man walked in the sun for a few minutes with the young man.
a2.ru: Старик несколько минут гулял на солнце вместе с юношей.

a2.en: They were both beautiful in different ways.
a2.ru: Они оба были прекрасны, каждый по-своему.

a2.en: The old man had white hair and a kind face.
a2.ru: У старика были седые волосы и доброе лицо.

a2.en: The young man was tall and handsome, but his eyes were very sad.
a2.ru: Юноша был высоким и красивым, но глаза у него были очень грустные.

a2.en: Then the old man went back into the house, and the young man went to work in the fields again.
a2.ru: Потом старик вернулся в дом, а юноша снова пошёл работать в поле.

a2.en: Night came, but the family had candles, so they had light.
a2.ru: Наступила ночь, но у семьи были свечи, и у них был свет.

a2.en: I was very happy because I could watch them in the evening, too.
a2.ru: Я очень обрадовался, потому что мог смотреть на них и вечером.

a2.en: The young people did things that I didn’t understand.
a2.ru: Молодые люди делали то, чего я не понимал.

a2.en: The old man played his beautiful music again.
a2.ru: Старик снова играл свою прекрасную музыку.

a2.en: Then the young man made some strange sounds.
a2.ru: Потом юноша стал издавать какие-то странные звуки.

a2.en: Later I learned that he was reading a book to them, but then I didn’t know about words or letters.
a2.ru: Позже я узнал, что он читал им книгу, но тогда я ничего не знал о словах и буквах.

a2.en: Soon the family put out the candles and went to bed.
a2.ru: Скоро семья погасила свечи и легла спать.

sub: Hidden in his hovel, the creature watches the poor but loving cottagers — blind old man, Felix and Agatha — through the winter, secretly helps them, begins to learn their language, sees his own hideous reflection, and greets the spring with hope

o: “I lay on my straw, but I could not sleep. I thought of the occurrences of the day. What chiefly struck me was the gentle manners of these people, and I longed to join them, but dared not. I remembered too well the treatment I had suffered the night before from the barbarous villagers, and resolved, whatever course of conduct I might hereafter think it right to pursue, that for the present I would remain quietly in my hovel, watching and endeavouring to discover the motives which influenced their actions.

“The cottagers arose the next morning before the sun. The young woman arranged the cottage and prepared the food, and the youth departed after the first meal.

“This day was passed in the same routine as that which preceded it. The young man was constantly employed out of doors, and the girl in various laborious occupations within. The old man, whom I soon perceived to be blind, employed his leisure hours on his instrument or in contemplation. Nothing could exceed the love and respect which the younger cottagers exhibited towards their venerable companion. They performed towards him every little office of affection and duty with gentleness, and he rewarded them by his benevolent smiles.

“They were not entirely happy. The young man and his companion often went apart and appeared to weep. I saw no cause for their unhappiness, but I was deeply affected by it. If such lovely creatures were miserable, it was less strange that I, an imperfect and solitary being, should be wretched. Yet why were these gentle beings unhappy? They possessed a delightful house (for such it was in my eyes) and every luxury; they had a fire to warm them when chill and delicious viands when hungry; they were dressed in excellent clothes; and, still more, they enjoyed one another’s company and speech, interchanging each day looks of affection and kindness. What did their tears imply? Did they really express pain? I was at first unable to solve these questions, but perpetual attention and time explained to me many appearances which were at first enigmatic.

“A considerable period elapsed before I discovered one of the causes of the uneasiness of this amiable family: it was poverty, and they suffered that evil in a very distressing degree. Their nourishment consisted entirely of the vegetables of their garden and the milk of one cow, which gave very little during the winter, when its masters could scarcely procure food to support it. They often, I believe, suffered the pangs of hunger very poignantly, especially the two younger cottagers, for several times they placed food before the old man when they reserved none for themselves.

“This trait of kindness moved me sensibly. I had been accustomed, during the night, to steal a part of their store for my own consumption, but when I found that in doing this I inflicted pain on the cottagers, I abstained and satisfied myself with berries, nuts, and roots which I gathered from a neighbouring wood.

“I discovered also another means through which I was enabled to assist their labours. I found that the youth spent a great part of each day in collecting wood for the family fire, and during the night I often took his tools, the use of which I quickly discovered, and brought home firing sufficient for the consumption of several days.

“I remember, the first time that I did this, the young woman, when she opened the door in the morning, appeared greatly astonished on seeing a great pile of wood on the outside. She uttered some words in a loud voice, and the youth joined her, who also expressed surprise. I observed, with pleasure, that he did not go to the forest that day, but spent it in repairing the cottage and cultivating the garden.

“By degrees I made a discovery of still greater moment. I found that these people possessed a method of communicating their experience and feelings to one another by articulate sounds. I perceived that the words they spoke sometimes produced pleasure or pain, smiles or sadness, in the minds and countenances of the hearers. This was indeed a godlike science, and I ardently desired to become acquainted with it. But I was baffled in every attempt I made for this purpose. Their pronunciation was quick, and the words they uttered, not having any apparent connection with visible objects, I was unable to discover any clue by which I could unravel the mystery of their reference.

By great application, however, and after having remained during the space of several revolutions of the moon in my hovel, I discovered the names that were given to some of the most familiar objects of discourse; I learned and applied the words, fire, milk, bread, and wood. I learned also the names of the cottagers themselves. The youth and his companion had each of them several names, but the old man had only one, which was father. The girl was called sister or Agatha, and the youth Felix, brother, or son. I cannot describe the delight I felt when I learned the ideas appropriated to each of these sounds and was able to pronounce them. I distinguished several other words without being able as yet to understand or apply them, such as good, dearest, unhappy.

“I spent the winter in this manner. The gentle manners and beauty of the cottagers greatly endeared them to me; when they were unhappy, I felt depressed; when they rejoiced, I sympathised in their joys. I saw few human beings besides them, and if any other happened to enter the cottage, their harsh manners and rude gait only enhanced to me the superior accomplishments of my friends.

The old man, I could perceive, often endeavoured to encourage his children, as sometimes I found that he called them, to cast off their melancholy. He would talk in a cheerful accent, with an expression of goodness that bestowed pleasure even upon me. Agatha listened with respect, her eyes sometimes filled with tears, which she endeavoured to wipe away unperceived; but I generally found that her countenance and tone were more cheerful after having listened to the exhortations of her father. It was not thus with Felix. He was always the saddest of the group, and even to my unpractised senses, he appeared to have suffered more deeply than his friends. But if his countenance was more sorrowful, his voice was more cheerful than that of his sister, especially when he addressed the old man.

“I could mention innumerable instances which, although slight, marked the dispositions of these amiable cottagers. In the midst of poverty and want, Felix carried with pleasure to his sister the first little white flower that peeped out from beneath the snowy ground. Early in the morning, before she had risen, he cleared away the snow that obstructed her path to the milk-house, drew water from the well, and brought the wood from the outhouse, where, to his perpetual astonishment, he found his store always replenished by an invisible hand. In the day, I believe, he worked sometimes for a neighbouring farmer, because he often went forth and did not return until dinner, yet brought no wood with him. At other times he worked in the garden, but as there was little to do in the frosty season, he read to the old man and Agatha.

“This reading had puzzled me extremely at first, but by degrees I discovered that he uttered many of the same sounds when he read as when he talked. I conjectured, therefore, that he found on the paper signs for speech which he understood, and I ardently longed to comprehend these also; but how was that possible when I did not even understand the sounds for which they stood as signs? I improved, however, sensibly in this science, but not sufficiently to follow up any kind of conversation, although I applied my whole mind to the endeavour, for I easily perceived that, although I eagerly longed to discover myself to the cottagers, I ought not to make the attempt until I had first become master of their language, which knowledge might enable me to make them overlook the deformity of my figure, for with this also the contrast perpetually presented to my eyes had made me acquainted.

“I had admired the perfect forms of my cottagers—their grace, beauty, and delicate complexions; but how was I terrified when I viewed myself in a transparent pool! At first I started back, unable to believe that it was indeed I who was reflected in the mirror; and when I became fully convinced that I was in reality the monster that I am, I was filled with the bitterest sensations of despondence and mortification. Alas! I did not yet entirely know the fatal effects of this miserable deformity.

“As the sun became warmer and the light of day longer, the snow vanished, and I beheld the bare trees and the black earth. From this time Felix was more employed, and the heart-moving indications of impending famine disappeared. Their food, as I afterwards found, was coarse, but it was wholesome; and they procured a sufficiency of it. Several new kinds of plants sprang up in the garden, which they dressed; and these signs of comfort increased daily as the season advanced.

“The old man, leaning on his son, walked each day at noon, when it did not rain, as I found it was called when the heavens poured forth its waters. This frequently took place, but a high wind quickly dried the earth, and the season became far more pleasant than it had been.

“My mode of life in my hovel was uniform. During the morning I attended the motions of the cottagers, and when they were dispersed in various occupations, I slept; the remainder of the day was spent in observing my friends. When they had retired to rest, if there was any moon or the night was star-light, I went into the woods and collected my own food and fuel for the cottage. When I returned, as often as it was necessary, I cleared their path from the snow and performed those offices that I had seen done by Felix. I afterwards found that these labours, performed by an invisible hand, greatly astonished them; and once or twice I heard them, on these occasions, utter the words good spirit, wonderful; but I did not then understand the signification of these terms.

“My thoughts now became more active, and I longed to discover the motives and feelings of these lovely creatures; I was inquisitive to know why Felix appeared so miserable and Agatha so sad. I thought (foolish wretch!) that it might be in my power to restore happiness to these deserving people. When I slept or was absent, the forms of the venerable blind father, the gentle Agatha, and the excellent Felix flitted before me. I looked upon them as superior beings who would be the arbiters of my future destiny. I formed in my imagination a thousand pictures of presenting myself to them, and their reception of me. I imagined that they would be disgusted, until, by my gentle demeanour and conciliating words, I should first win their favour and afterwards their love.

“These thoughts exhilarated me and led me to apply with fresh ardour to the acquiring the art of language. My organs were indeed harsh, but supple; and although my voice was very unlike the soft music of their tones, yet I pronounced such words as I understood with tolerable ease. It was as the ass and the lap-dog; yet surely the gentle ass whose intentions were affectionate, although his manners were rude, deserved better treatment than blows and execration.

“The pleasant showers and genial warmth of spring greatly altered the aspect of the earth. Men who before this change seemed to have been hid in caves dispersed themselves and were employed in various arts of cultivation. The birds sang in more cheerful notes, and the leaves began to bud forth on the trees. Happy, happy earth! Fit habitation for gods, which, so short a time before, was bleak, damp, and unwholesome. My spirits were elevated by the enchanting appearance of nature; the past was blotted from my memory, the present was tranquil, and the future gilded by bright rays of hope and anticipations of joy.”

What struck me most was the gentle manners of these people, and I longed to join them, but I did not dare. I remembered only too well how the savage villagers had treated me the night before, so I decided that, whatever I might later think it right to do, for the moment I would stay quietly in my hovel, watching them and trying to understand what made them act as they did.

“The cottagers got up the next morning before sunrise. The young woman tidied the cottage and made the food, and the young man left after the first meal. “This day followed the same routine as the day before. The young man was always busy outdoors, and the girl did various tiring jobs inside. The old man, who I soon realised was blind, spent his free hours playing his instrument or lost in thought. Nothing could be greater than the love and respect that the two younger cottagers showed their elderly companion. They gently did every small service of love and duty for him, and he rewarded them with his kind smiles.

“They were not completely happy. The young man and his companion often went off alone and seemed to cry. I could see no reason for their sadness, but it moved me deeply. If such lovely creatures were miserable, it was less surprising that I, an imperfect and lonely being, should be wretched. Yet why were these gentle beings unhappy? They had a lovely house (or so it seemed to me) and every luxury; they had a fire to warm them when they were cold and delicious food when they were hungry; they wore excellent clothes; and, what is more, they enjoyed each other’s company and conversation, exchanging looks of love and kindness every day. What did their tears mean? Were they really a sign of pain? At first I could not answer these questions, but constant watching and time explained many things to me that had at first been a mystery.

“Quite a long time passed before I discovered one of the reasons for this kind family’s distress: it was poverty, and they suffered from it terribly. Their food consisted only of vegetables from their garden and the milk of one cow, which gave very little in winter, when its owners could hardly find enough food to keep it alive. I believe they often felt the sharp pangs of hunger, especially the two younger ones, because several times they put food in front of the old man when they had kept none for themselves.

“This act of kindness touched me deeply. I had got into the habit of stealing part of their food at night for myself, but when I realised that I was causing the cottagers pain by doing this, I stopped and made do with berries, nuts and roots that I gathered in a nearby wood.

“I also found another way to help them with their work. I noticed that the young man spent a large part of every day collecting wood for the family fire, so at night I often took his tools, which I quickly learned to use, and brought back enough firewood to last several days.

“I remember that the first time I did this, the young woman opened the door in the morning and looked amazed to see a great pile of wood outside. She called out some words loudly, and the young man joined her and was surprised too. I was pleased to see that he did not go to the forest that day but spent it repairing the cottage and working in the garden.

“Gradually I made an even more important discovery. I found that these people had a way of sharing their experiences and feelings with one another through spoken sounds. I noticed that the words they spoke sometimes caused pleasure or pain, smiles or sadness, in the minds and faces of those who heard them. This was truly a godlike science, and I passionately wanted to learn it. But every attempt I made was frustrated. They spoke quickly, and since the words they said had no obvious connection with things I could see, I could find no clue to help me solve the mystery of what they meant.

However, by working very hard, and after staying in my hovel for several months, I learned the names of some of the things they talked about most often; I learned and used the words fire, milk, bread and wood. I also learned the names of the cottagers themselves. The young man and his companion each had several names, but the old man had only one, which was father. The girl was called sister or Agatha, and the young man Felix, brother or son. I cannot describe my delight when I understood the ideas that belonged to each of these sounds and was able to say them. I could make out several other words without yet being able to understand or use them, such as good, dearest and unhappy.

“This is how I spent the winter. The cottagers’ gentle manners and beauty made me grow very fond of them; when they were unhappy, I felt low, and when they were joyful, I shared their joy. I saw few other people, and if anyone else happened to come into the cottage, their rough manners and clumsy walk only made my friends’ superior qualities stand out more clearly to me.

I could see that the old man often tried to encourage his children, as I discovered he sometimes called them, to shake off their sadness. He would speak in a cheerful tone, with a look of such goodness that it gave pleasure even to me. Agatha listened respectfully, her eyes sometimes filling with tears, which she tried to wipe away without being noticed; but I usually found that her face and voice were more cheerful after she had listened to her father’s advice. It was not like this with Felix. He was always the saddest of them, and even to my inexperienced senses, he seemed to have suffered more deeply than the others. But although his face was sadder, his voice was more cheerful than his sister’s, especially when he spoke to the old man.

“I could mention countless small examples that showed the character of these kind cottagers. In the middle of poverty and need, Felix happily brought his sister the first little white flower that peeped out from under the snowy ground. Early in the morning, before she was up, he cleared away the snow that blocked her path to the milk-house, drew water from the well and fetched wood from the shed, where, to his constant amazement, he always found the pile refilled by an invisible hand. During the day, I believe, he sometimes worked for a nearby farmer, because he often went out and did not come back until dinner, yet brought no wood with him. At other times he worked in the garden, but as there was little to do in the frosty season, he read to the old man and Agatha.

“At first this reading puzzled me enormously, but gradually I discovered that he made many of the same sounds when he read as when he talked. When they had gone to bed, if there was a moon or the night was starlit, I went into the woods and gathered my own food and fuel for the cottage. I imagined that they would be disgusted at first, until my gentle behaviour and soothing words won first their approval and then their love.

“These thoughts thrilled me and made me throw myself into learning language with new enthusiasm.
