b1.ru: Несколько дней я оставался рядом с местом, где всё это случилось.

b1.en: Sometimes I wanted to see you; sometimes I wanted to leave the world and its pain for ever.
b1.ru: Иногда я хотел увидеть тебя, иногда — навсегда покинуть мир и его боль.

b1.en: At last I came to these mountains, and I have wandered through them, burning with a desire that only you can satisfy.
b1.ru: Наконец я пришёл в эти горы и бродил по ним, сгорая от желания, которое можешь исполнить только ты.

b1.en: We will not part until you promise to do what I ask.
b1.ru: Мы не расстанемся, пока ты не пообещаешь выполнить мою просьбу.

b1.en: I am alone and unhappy.
b1.ru: Я одинок и несчастен.

b1.en: People will not be with me.
b1.ru: Люди не хотят быть со мной.

b1.en: But a woman who is as ugly and horrible as I am would not say no to me.
b1.ru: Но женщина, такая же уродливая и страшная, как я, не отказала бы мне.

b1.en: My companion must be the same kind of creature as me, with the same faults.
b1.ru: Моя подруга должна быть таким же существом, как я, с теми же недостатками.

b1.en: You must make this creature for me.”
b1.ru: Ты должен создать для меня это существо».

a2.en: “Oh, creator, I hate you!
a2.ru: «О создатель, я ненавижу тебя!

a2.en: Why did I not die at that moment?
a2.ru: Почему я не умер в тот момент?

a2.en: You gave me life, but you did not care about me.
a2.ru: Ты дал мне жизнь, но тебе было всё равно, что со мной будет.

a2.en: I did not feel sad yet.
a2.ru: Грусти я ещё не чувствовал.

a2.en: I only felt very angry, and I wanted revenge.
a2.ru: Я только очень злился и хотел отомстить.

a2.en: I wanted to destroy the cottage and the people in it.
a2.ru: Я хотел уничтожить хижину и людей в ней.

a2.en: I wanted to hear them scream.
a2.ru: Я хотел слышать, как они кричат.

a2.en: “At night I left my hiding place and walked in the forest.
a2.ru: Ночью я вышел из укрытия и пошёл по лесу.

a2.en: Now I was not afraid of people, so I cried out loudly in pain, like an animal.
a2.ru: Теперь я не боялся людей и громко кричал от боли, как зверь.

a2.en: I ran through the forest very fast, like a wild animal, and I broke everything in my way.
a2.ru: Я очень быстро бежал по лесу, как дикий зверь, и ломал всё на своём пути.

a2.en: It was a terrible night!
a2.ru: Это была ужасная ночь!

a2.en: The cold stars shone above me, and the trees moved in the wind.
a2.ru: Надо мной светили холодные звёзды, деревья качались на ветру.

a2.en: Sometimes a bird sang.
a2.ru: Иногда пела птица.

a2.en: Everyone was resting or happy, but not me.
a2.ru: Все отдыхали или были счастливы, но не я.

a2.en: I felt like the devil.
a2.ru: Я чувствовал себя дьяволом.

a2.en: I wanted to pull up the trees and destroy everything around me.
a2.ru: Я хотел вырывать деревья и разрушить всё вокруг.

a2.en: “But after some time I was very tired.
a2.ru: Но через некоторое время я очень устал.

a2.en: I fell down on the wet grass.
a2.ru: Я упал на мокрую траву.

a2.en: There were millions of people in the world, but nobody wanted to help me.
a2.ru: На свете были миллионы людей, но никто не хотел мне помочь.

a2.en: So why should I be kind to them?
a2.ru: Так почему я должен быть к ним добр?

a2.en: From that moment, I was at war with all people – and most of all with you, because you made me.
a2.ru: С этой минуты я воевал со всеми людьми — и больше всего с тобой, потому что ты меня создал.

a2.en: “The sun came up.
a2.ru: Взошло солнце.

a2.en: I heard people’s voices, so I could not go back to my hiding place.
a2.ru: Я услышал голоса людей, поэтому не мог вернуться в своё укрытие.

a2.en: I hid in some bushes and thought about my situation.
a2.ru: Я спрятался в кустах и думал о своём положении.

a2.en: “The sun and the fresh air made me calmer.
a2.ru: Солнце и свежий воздух успокоили меня.

a2.en: I thought about the cottage again, and I understood that I was too quick.
a2.ru: Я снова подумал о хижине и понял, что поторопился.

a2.en: It was my mistake.
a2.ru: Это была моя ошибка.

a2.en: The old father liked me, but I showed myself to his children, and they were afraid.
a2.ru: Старый отец хорошо ко мне отнёсся, но я показался его детям, и они испугались.

a2.en: I should wait and be friends with old De Lacey first.
a2.ru: Мне надо было подождать и сначала подружиться со старым Де Лэси.

a2.en: Then he could tell his family about me.
a2.ru: Потом он мог бы рассказать обо мне своей семье.

a2.en: I decided to go back and talk to the old man again.
a2.ru: Я решил вернуться и снова поговорить со стариком.

a2.en: “After that I felt calmer, and in the afternoon I slept.
a2.ru: После этого мне стало спокойнее, и днём я заснул.

a2.en: But I had bad dreams.
a2.ru: Но мне снились плохие сны.

a2.en: I saw the terrible scene again: the women were running away, and angry Felix was pulling me away from his father.
a2.ru: Я снова видел ту ужасную сцену: женщины убегали, а сердитый Феликс оттаскивал меня от своего отца.

a2.en: When I woke up, it was night.
a2.ru: Когда я проснулся, была ночь.

a2.en: I went out and looked for food.
a2.ru: Я вышел и стал искать еду.

a2.en: “After I ate, I walked to the cottage.
a2.ru: Поев, я пошёл к хижине.

a2.en: Everything was quiet.
a2.ru: Всё было тихо.

a2.en: I went into my shed and waited for the family to get up.
a2.ru: Я зашёл в свой сарай и ждал, когда семья проснётся.

a2.en: But nobody came out, and the sun went up high in the sky.
a2.ru: Но никто не выходил, а солнце поднялось высоко в небе.

a2.en: I was very afraid.
a2.ru: Мне было очень страшно.

a2.en: It was dark in the cottage, and I heard nothing.
a2.ru: В хижине было темно, и я ничего не слышал.

a2.en: “Then two men walked past the cottage.
a2.ru: Потом мимо хижины прошли двое мужчин.

a2.en: They stopped and talked and moved their arms a lot.
a2.ru: Они остановились, поговорили и много размахивали руками.

a2.en: I did not understand them, because they spoke a different language.
a2.ru: Я их не понял, потому что они говорили на другом языке.

a2.en: Soon Felix came with another man.
a2.ru: Вскоре пришёл Феликс с другим человеком.

a2.en: I was surprised, and I listened carefully.
a2.ru: Я удивился и внимательно слушал.

a2.en: “The man said to Felix, ‘You must pay three months’ money for the house, and you will lose your vegetables.
a2.ru: Мужчина сказал Феликсу: „Вам придётся заплатить за дом за три месяца, и вы потеряете свои овощи.

a2.en: Please think about it for a few days.’
a2.ru: Пожалуйста, подумайте несколько дней“.

a2.en: “‘No,’ said Felix; ‘we can never live here again.
a2.ru: „Нет, — сказал Феликс, — мы больше никогда не сможем здесь жить.

a2.en: My father is in danger because of the terrible thing that happened.
a2.ru: Мой отец в опасности из-за того ужасного, что случилось.

a2.en: My wife and my sister are still very afraid.
a2.ru: Моя жена и сестра всё ещё очень напуганы.

a2.en: Please take your house back.
a2.ru: Пожалуйста, заберите свой дом.

a2.en: I want to leave this place.’
a2.ru: Я хочу уехать отсюда“.

a2.en: “Felix was shaking.
a2.ru: Феликс дрожал.

a2.en: The two men went into the cottage for a few minutes, and then they left.
a2.ru: Двое мужчин зашли в хижину на несколько минут, а потом ушли.

a2.en: I never saw the De Lacey family again.
a2.ru: Больше я никогда не видел семью Де Лэси.

a2.en: “I stayed in my shed all day.
a2.ru: Я весь день просидел в своём сарае.

a2.en: I felt terrible.
a2.ru: Мне было ужасно.

a2.en: My friends were gone.
a2.ru: Мои друзья ушли.

a2.en: They were the only people in my life.
a2.ru: Они были единственными людьми в моей жизни.

a2.en: For the first time, I felt hate, and I wanted to hurt people.
a2.ru: Впервые я почувствовал ненависть и захотел причинять людям боль.

a2.en: Then I thought about De Lacey’s kind voice, Agatha’s gentle eyes and beautiful Safie, and I cried.
a2.ru: Потом я вспомнил добрый голос Де Лэси, нежные глаза Агаты и красавицу Сафию и заплакал.

a2.en: But then I remembered that they left me, and I was angry again.
a2.ru: Но потом я вспомнил, что они меня бросили, и снова разозлился.

a2.en: I could not hurt people, so I decided to hurt things.
a2.ru: Я не мог навредить людям, поэтому решил навредить вещам.

a2.en: In the evening I put a lot of dry wood and straw around the cottage.
a2.ru: Вечером я положил вокруг хижины много сухих дров и соломы.

a2.en: I destroyed the garden, and I waited for the moon to go down.
a2.ru: Я уничтожил огород и ждал, когда зайдёт луна.

a2.en: “Later a strong wind came and blew the clouds away.
a2.ru: Позже поднялся сильный ветер и разогнал облака.

a2.en: The wind made me feel crazy.
a2.ru: От ветра я словно сошёл с ума.

a2.en: I lit a dry branch and danced around the cottage.
a2.ru: Я зажёг сухую ветку и плясал вокруг хижины.

a2.en: I watched the moon in the west.
a2.ru: Я смотрел на луну на западе.

a2.en: When the moon went down, I screamed and set fire to the straw and the bushes.
a2.ru: Когда луна зашла, я закричал и поджёг солому и кусты.

a2.en: The wind helped the fire, and soon the cottage was burning.
a2.ru: Ветер помог огню, и скоро хижина горела.

a2.en: “When I was sure that nobody could save the house, I ran into the woods.
a2.ru: Когда я убедился, что никто не спасёт дом, я убежал в лес.

a2.en: “Now I could go anywhere in the world.
a2.ru: Теперь я мог пойти куда угодно.

a2.en: But where?
a2.ru: Но куда?

a2.en: People hated me in every country.
a2.ru: Люди ненавидели меня в любой стране.

a2.en: Then I thought of you.
a2.ru: Потом я подумал о тебе.

a2.en: I knew from your papers that you were my father, my creator.
a2.ru: Из твоих бумаг я знал, что ты мой отец, мой создатель.

a2.en: You gave me life, so you should help me!
a2.ru: Ты дал мне жизнь, значит, ты должен мне помочь!

a2.en: Felix taught Safie about the countries of the world, and I learned too.
a2.ru: Феликс рассказывал Сафии о странах мира, и я тоже учился.

a2.en: You wrote that you came from Geneva, so I decided to go there.
a2.ru: Ты писал, что ты из Женевы, поэтому я решил пойти туда.

a2.en: “But how could I find the way?
a2.ru: Но как мне было найти дорогу?

a2.en: I knew that I had to go south-west, and I followed the sun.
a2.ru: Я знал, что мне нужно идти на юго-запад, и шёл за солнцем.

a2.en: I did not know the names of the towns, and I could not ask people.
a2.ru: Я не знал названий городов и не мог спрашивать людей.

a2.en: Only you could help me, but I hated you.
a2.ru: Только ты мог мне помочь, но я тебя ненавидел.

a2.en: You were a cruel creator!
a2.ru: Ты был жестоким создателем!

a2.en: You gave me feelings, and then you left me alone in a world where everyone hated me.
a2.ru: Ты дал мне чувства, а потом оставил меня одного в мире, где все меня ненавидели.

a2.en: But you had to help me.
a2.ru: Но ты был обязан мне помочь.

a2.en: Nobody else would.
a2.ru: Больше никто бы не помог.

a2.en: “It was a long, hard journey.
a2.ru: Это был долгий, тяжёлый путь.

a2.en: I left in late autumn.
a2.ru: Я ушёл поздней осенью.

a2.en: I only walked at night, because I did not want to meet people.
a2.ru: Я шёл только ночью, потому что не хотел встречать людей.

a2.en: It was cold.
a2.ru: Было холодно.

a2.en: It rained and snowed, and the rivers froze.
a2.ru: Шёл дождь и снег, реки замёрзли.

a2.en: I had no house to sleep in.
a2.ru: Мне негде было спать.

a2.en: Oh, how often I cursed you!
a2.ru: О, как часто я проклинал тебя!

a2.en: I was not gentle any more.
a2.ru: Я больше не был добрым.

a2.en: I was bitter and angry.
a2.ru: Я был полон горечи и злобы.

a2.en: The nearer I came to you, the more I wanted revenge.
a2.ru: Чем ближе я подходил к тебе, тем сильнее хотел отомстить.

a2.en: It snowed, but I did not stop.
a2.ru: Шёл снег, но я не останавливался.

a2.en: I had a map, but I often got lost.
a2.ru: У меня была карта, но я часто сбивался с пути.

a2.en: I was always angry and unhappy.
a2.ru: Я всегда был зол и несчастен.

a2.en: And when I came to Switzerland in the spring, something happened that made me even angrier.
a2.ru: А когда весной я пришёл в Швейцарию, случилось то, что разозлило меня ещё сильнее.

a2.en: “I usually slept in the day and walked at night.
a2.ru: Обычно я спал днём и шёл ночью.

a2.en: But one morning I was in a big forest, so I walked on in the daytime.
a2.ru: Но однажды утром я был в большом лесу, поэтому продолжил путь днём.

a2.en: It was one of the first days of spring.
a2.ru: Это был один из первых весенних дней.

a2.en: The sun was warm, and the air was soft.
a2.ru: Солнце было тёплым, а воздух — мягким.

a2.en: For the first time in a long time, I felt kind and happy.
a2.ru: Впервые за долгое время я почувствовал себя добрым и счастливым.

a2.en: I forgot that I was alone and ugly.
a2.ru: Я забыл, что я одинок и уродлив.

a2.en: I cried a little, and I thanked the sun for this joy.
a2.ru: Я немного поплакал и поблагодарил солнце за эту радость.

a2.en: “I came to the end of the forest.
a2.ru: Я дошёл до края леса.

a2.en: There was a deep, fast river there.
a2.ru: Там текла глубокая быстрая река.

a2.en: Then I heard voices, and I hid behind a tree.
a2.ru: Потом я услышал голоса и спрятался за дерево.

a2.en: A young girl ran towards me.
a2.ru: Ко мне подбежала молодая девушка.

a2.en: She was laughing and playing a game.
a2.ru: Она смеялась и играла.

a2.en: She ran near the river, and suddenly she fell into the water.
a2.ru: Она бежала у реки и вдруг упала в воду.

a2.en: I ran out and jumped into the river.
a2.ru: Я выбежал и прыгнул в реку.

a2.en: It was very hard, but I saved her and pulled her out.
a2.ru: Это было очень трудно, но я спас её и вытащил.

a2.en: She was not moving, and I tried to help her.
a2.ru: Она не двигалась, и я пытался ей помочь.

a2.en: Then a man came.
a2.ru: Тут подошёл мужчина.

a2.en: He was her friend in the game.
a2.ru: Это был её друг по игре.

a2.en: He saw me, took the girl from my arms and ran into the forest.
a2.ru: Он увидел меня, выхватил девушку из моих рук и побежал в лес.

a2.en: I followed him.
a2.ru: Я пошёл за ним.

a2.en: But he turned, pointed his gun at me and shot me.
a2.ru: Но он обернулся, направил на меня ружьё и выстрелил.

a2.en: I fell down, and the man ran away.
a2.ru: Я упал, а мужчина убежал.

a2.en: “This was my thank-you for being kind!
a2.ru: Вот какое спасибо я получил за доброту!

a2.en: I saved a girl’s life, and now I was in terrible pain.
a2.ru: Я спас девушке жизнь, а теперь мне было ужасно больно.

a2.en: A few minutes before, I was kind and gentle.
a2.ru: Несколько минут назад я был добрым и нежным.

a2.en: Now I was full of hate.
a2.ru: Теперь я был полон ненависти.

a2.en: I promised to hate all people for ever and to take revenge on them.
a2.ru: Я поклялся вечно ненавидеть всех людей и мстить им.

a2.en: Then the pain was too strong, and I fainted.
a2.ru: Потом боль стала слишком сильной, и я потерял сознание.

a2.en: “For some weeks I lived in the woods and tried to make my wound better.
a2.ru: Несколько недель я жил в лесу и пытался вылечить рану.

a2.en: The bullet was in my shoulder, and I could not take it out.
a2.ru: Пуля была у меня в плече, и я не мог её вынуть.

a2.en: It was so unfair!
a2.ru: Это было так несправедливо!

a2.en: This made my pain worse.
a2.ru: От этого боль была ещё сильнее.

a2.en: Every day I promised myself a terrible revenge.
a2.ru: Каждый день я обещал себе страшную месть.

a2.en: “After some weeks my wound was better, and I walked on.
a2.ru: Через несколько недель рана зажила, и я пошёл дальше.

a2.en: The sun and the spring wind did not make me happy now.
a2.ru: Солнце и весенний ветер теперь меня не радовали.

a2.en: I knew that I could never be happy.
a2.ru: Я знал, что никогда не смогу быть счастливым.

a2.en: “Two months later, I arrived near Geneva.
a2.ru: Через два месяца я добрался до окрестностей Женевы.

a2.en: “It was evening.
a2.ru: Был вечер.

a2.en: I hid in the fields near the city.
a2.ru: Я спрятался в полях у города.

a2.en: I wanted to think about how to speak to you.
a2.ru: Я хотел подумать, как с тобой заговорить.

a2.en: I was tired, hungry and very unhappy.
a2.ru: Я был усталым, голодным и очень несчастным.

a2.en: “I slept a little.
a2.ru: Я немного поспал.

a2.en: Then a beautiful little boy ran into my hiding place.
a2.ru: Потом в моё укрытие вбежал красивый мальчик.

a2.en: He was playing.
a2.ru: Он играл.

a2.en: I looked at him, and I had an idea.
a2.ru: Я посмотрел на него, и мне пришла в голову мысль.

a2.en: He was very young.
a2.ru: Он был совсем маленький.

a2.en: Maybe he was not afraid of ugly people yet.
a2.ru: Может быть, он ещё не боялся некрасивых людей.

a2.en: I could take him and teach him.
a2.ru: Я мог бы взять его и учить.

a2.en: He could be my friend, and I would not be alone.
a2.ru: Он мог бы стать моим другом, и я не был бы одинок.

a2.en: “When the boy ran past me, I caught him.
a2.ru: Когда мальчик пробегал мимо, я поймал его.

a2.en: He saw me, covered his eyes and screamed.
a2.ru: Он увидел меня, закрыл глаза и закричал.

a2.en: I took his hand from his face and said, ‘Child, why are you screaming?
a2.ru: Я отвёл его руку от лица и сказал: „Дитя, почему ты кричишь?

a2.en: I will not hurt you.
a2.ru: Я тебя не обижу.

a2.en: Listen to me.’
a2.ru: Послушай меня“.

a2.en: “The boy fought me.
a2.ru: Мальчик вырывался.

a2.en: ‘Let me go!’ he cried.
a2.ru: „Пусти меня! — кричал он.

a2.en: ‘You are a monster!
a2.ru: — Ты чудовище!

a2.en: You want to eat me!
a2.ru: Ты хочешь меня съесть!

a2.en: Let me go, or I will tell my papa!’
a2.ru: Пусти, или я скажу папе!“

a2.en: “‘You will never see your father again.
a2.ru: „Ты больше никогда не увидишь своего отца.

a2.en: You must come with me.’
a2.ru: Ты пойдёшь со мной“.

a2.en: “‘Let me go, you ugly monster!
a2.ru: „Пусти меня, мерзкое чудовище!

a2.en: My papa is Mr Frankenstein, and he will punish you!’
a2.ru: Мой папа — господин Франкенштейн, и он тебя накажет!“

a2.en: “‘Frankenstein!
a2.ru: „Франкенштейн!

a2.en: So your family is my enemy’s family.
a2.ru: Значит, твоя семья — семья моего врага.

a2.en: You will be my first victim.’
a2.ru: Ты будешь моей первой жертвой“.

a2.en: “The boy fought and shouted bad names at me.
a2.ru: Мальчик вырывался и выкрикивал мне обидные слова.

a2.en: I put my hands on his throat to stop him.
a2.ru: Я сжал руками его горло, чтобы он замолчал.

a2.en: A moment later, he was dead.
a2.ru: Через мгновение он был мёртв.

a2.en: “I looked at him, and I was happy, like a devil.
a2.ru: Я смотрел на него и радовался, как дьявол.

a2.en: I clapped my hands.
a2.ru: Я хлопал в ладоши.

a2.en: I cried, ‘I can destroy too!
a2.ru: Я кричал: „Я тоже умею разрушать!

a2.en: This will hurt my enemy, and I will bring him many more troubles!’
a2.ru: Это ранит моего врага, и я принесу ему ещё много бед!“

a2.en: “Then I saw something shining on the boy’s chest.
a2.ru: Потом я увидел, что на груди мальчика что-то блестит.

a2.en: It was a small picture of a beautiful woman.
a2.ru: Это был маленький портрет красивой женщины.

a2.en: I liked it, and I felt softer for a moment.
a2.ru: Он мне понравился, и на минуту я смягчился.

a2.en: I looked at her dark eyes and her lovely face.
a2.ru: Я смотрел на её тёмные глаза и прелестное лицо.

a2.en: But then I was angry again.
a2.ru: Но потом я снова разозлился.

a2.en: A beautiful woman like this could never love me.
a2.ru: Такая красивая женщина никогда не смогла бы меня полюбить.

a2.en: If she saw me, she would be afraid and disgusted.
a2.ru: Если бы она меня увидела, ей стало бы страшно и противно.

a2.en: “Are you surprised that I was so angry?
a2.ru: Ты удивляешься, что я так разозлился?

a2.en: I am only surprised that I did not attack all the people in the world then.
a2.ru: Я удивляюсь лишь тому, что тогда я не напал на всех людей на свете.

a2.en: “I left the place of the murder and looked for a better hiding place.
a2.ru: Я ушёл с места убийства и стал искать укрытие получше.

a2.en: I went into a barn.
a2.ru: Я зашёл в сарай.

a2.en: I thought it was empty.
a2.ru: Я думал, что он пустой.

a2.en: But a young woman was sleeping there on some straw.
a2.ru: Но там на соломе спала молодая женщина.

a2.en: She was pretty and healthy.
a2.ru: Она была миловидной и здоровой.

a2.en: I thought, ‘She smiles at everyone, but never at me.’
a2.ru: Я подумал: „Она улыбается всем, но никогда — мне“.

a2.en: I bent over her and whispered, ‘Wake up, my beautiful love!’
a2.ru: Я склонился над ней и прошептал: „Проснись, моя прекрасная любовь!“

a2.en: “The woman moved, and I was afraid.
a2.ru: Женщина пошевелилась, и мне стало страшно.

a2.en: What if she woke up and saw me?
a2.ru: Что, если она проснётся и увидит меня?

a2.en: She would scream and tell everyone about the murderer.
a2.ru: Она закричит и расскажет всем об убийце.

a2.en: Then a terrible idea came to me.
a2.ru: Тогда мне в голову пришла ужасная мысль.

a2.en: She, not I, would be punished for the murder!
a2.ru: Её, а не меня, накажут за убийство!

a2.en: Felix’s lessons and the cruel laws of people taught me how to do this.
a2.ru: Уроки Феликса и жестокие законы людей научили меня, как это сделать.

a2.en: I put the picture in her dress.
a2.ru: Я положил портрет ей в платье.

a2.en: She moved again, and I ran away.
a2.ru: Она снова пошевелилась, и я убежал.

a2.en: “For some days I stayed near that place.
a2.ru: Несколько дней я оставался рядом с тем местом.

a2.en: Sometimes I wanted to see you, and sometimes I wanted to die.
a2.ru: Иногда я хотел увидеть тебя, а иногда хотел умереть.

a2.en: Then I came to these mountains.
a2.ru: Потом я пришёл в эти горы.

a2.en: I want something very much, and only you can give it to me.
a2.ru: Я очень сильно хочу одного, и только ты можешь мне это дать.

a2.en: We will not leave this place until you promise to help me.
a2.ru: Мы не уйдём отсюда, пока ты не пообещаешь мне помочь.

a2.en: I am alone and unhappy.
a2.ru: Я одинок и несчастен.

a2.en: People will not be my friends.
a2.ru: Люди не хотят со мной дружить.

a2.en: But a woman as ugly as me will not say no to me.
a2.ru: Но женщина, такая же уродливая, как я, мне не откажет.

a2.en: You must make a woman like me.”
a2.ru: Ты должен создать для меня такую же женщину, как я».

sub: The creature demands a female companion; Victor refuses, is moved by its pleas and threats, and finally agrees, then returns to Geneva burdened by his dreaded task

o:
The being finished speaking and fixed his looks upon me in the expectation of a reply. But I was bewildered, perplexed, and unable to arrange my ideas sufficiently to understand the full extent of his proposition. He continued,

“You must create a female for me with whom I can live in the interchange of those sympathies necessary for my being. This you alone can do, and I demand it of you as a right which you must not refuse to concede.”

The latter part of his tale had kindled anew in me the anger that had died away while he narrated his peaceful life among the cottagers, and as he said this I could no longer suppress the rage that burned within me.

“I do refuse it,” I replied; “and no torture shall ever extort a consent from me. You may render me the most miserable of men, but you shall never make me base in my own eyes. Shall I create another like yourself, whose joint wickedness might desolate the world. Begone! I have answered you; you may torture me, but I will never consent.”

“You are in the wrong,” replied the fiend; “and instead of threatening, I am content to reason with you. I am malicious because I am miserable. Am I not shunned and hated by all mankind? You, my creator, would tear me to pieces and triumph; remember that, and tell me why I should pity man more than he pities me? You would not call it murder if you could precipitate me into one of those ice-rifts and destroy my frame, the work of your own hands.

Shall I respect man when he condemns me? Let him live with me in the interchange of kindness, and instead of injury I would bestow every benefit upon him with tears of gratitude at his acceptance. But that cannot be; the human senses are insurmountable barriers to our union. Yet mine shall not be the submission of abject slavery. I will revenge my injuries; if I cannot inspire love, I will cause fear, and chiefly towards you my arch-enemy, because my creator, do I swear inextinguishable hatred. Have a care; I will work at your destruction, nor finish until I desolate your heart, so that you shall curse the hour of your birth.”

A fiendish rage animated him as he said this; his face was wrinkled into contortions too horrible for human eyes to behold; but presently he calmed himself and proceeded—

“I intended to reason. This passion is detrimental to me, for you do not reflect that you are the cause of its excess. If any being felt emotions of benevolence towards me, I should return them a hundred and a hundredfold; for that one creature’s sake I would make peace with the whole kind! But I now indulge in dreams of bliss that cannot be realised.

What I ask of you is reasonable and moderate; I demand a creature of another sex, but as hideous as myself; the gratification is small, but it is all that I can receive, and it shall content me. It is true, we shall be monsters, cut off from all the world; but on that account we shall be more attached to one another. Our lives will not be happy, but they will be harmless and free from the misery I now feel. Oh! My creator, make me happy; let me feel gratitude towards you for one benefit! Let me see that I excite the sympathy of some existing thing; do not deny me my request!”

I was moved. I shuddered when I thought of the possible consequences of my consent, but I felt that there was some justice in his argument. His tale and the feelings he now expressed proved him to be a creature of fine sensations, and did I not as his maker owe him all the portion of happiness that it was in my power to bestow? He saw my change of feeling and continued,

“If you consent, neither you nor any other human being shall ever see us again; I will go to the vast wilds of South America. My food is not that of man; I do not destroy the lamb and the kid to glut my appetite; acorns and berries afford me sufficient nourishment. My companion will be of the same nature as myself and will be content with the same fare. We shall make our bed of dried leaves; the sun will shine on us as on man and will ripen our food. The picture I present to you is peaceful and human, and you must feel that you could deny it only in the wantonness of power and cruelty. Pitiless as you have been towards me, I now see compassion in your eyes; let me seize the favourable moment and persuade you to promise what I so ardently desire.”

“You propose,” replied I, “to fly from the habitations of man, to dwell in those wilds where the beasts of the field will be your only companions. How can you, who long for the love and sympathy of man, persevere in this exile? You will return and again seek their kindness, and you will meet with their detestation; your evil passions will be renewed, and you will then have a companion to aid you in the task of destruction. This may not be; cease to argue the point, for I cannot consent.”

“How inconstant are your feelings! But a moment ago you were moved by my representations, and why do you again harden yourself to my complaints? I swear to you, by the earth which I inhabit, and by you that made me, that with the companion you bestow, I will quit the neighbourhood of man and dwell, as it may chance, in the most savage of places. My evil passions will have fled, for I shall meet with sympathy! My life will flow quietly away, and in my dying moments I shall not curse my maker.”

His words had a strange effect upon me. I compassionated him and sometimes felt a wish to console him, but when I looked upon him, when I saw the filthy mass that moved and talked, my heart sickened and my feelings were altered to those of horror and hatred. I tried to stifle these sensations; I thought that as I could not sympathise with him, I had no right to withhold from him the small portion of happiness which was yet in my power to bestow.

“You swear,” I said, “to be harmless; but have you not already shown a degree of malice that should reasonably make me distrust you? May not even this be a feint that will increase your triumph by affording a wider scope for your revenge?”

“How is this? I must not be trifled with, and I demand an answer. If I have no ties and no affections, hatred and vice must be my portion; the love of another will destroy the cause of my crimes, and I shall become a thing of whose existence everyone will be ignorant. My vices are the children of a forced solitude that I abhor, and my virtues will necessarily arise when I live in communion with an equal. I shall feel the affections of a sensitive being and become linked to the chain of existence and events from which I am now excluded.”

I paused some time to reflect on all he had related and the various arguments which he had employed. I thought of the promise of virtues which he had displayed on the opening of his existence and the subsequent blight of all kindly feeling by the loathing and scorn which his protectors had manifested towards him. His power and threats were not omitted in my calculations; a creature who could exist in the ice-caves of the glaciers and hide himself from pursuit among the ridges of inaccessible precipices was a being possessing faculties it would be vain to cope with. After a long pause of reflection I concluded that the justice due both to him and my fellow creatures demanded of me that I should comply with his request. Turning to him, therefore, I said,

“I consent to your demand, on your solemn oath to quit Europe for ever, and every other place in the neighbourhood of man, as soon as I shall deliver into your hands a female who will accompany you in your exile.”

“I swear,” he cried, “by the sun, and by the blue sky of heaven, and by the fire of love that burns my heart, that if you grant my prayer, while they exist you shall never behold me again. Depart to your home and commence your labours; I shall watch their progress with unutterable anxiety; and fear not but that when you are ready I shall appear.”

Saying this, he suddenly quitted me, fearful, perhaps, of any change in my sentiments. I saw him descend the mountain with greater speed than the flight of an eagle, and quickly lost among the undulations of the sea of ice.

His tale had occupied the whole day, and the sun was upon the verge of the horizon when he departed. I knew that I ought to hasten my descent towards the valley, as I should soon be encompassed in darkness; but my heart was heavy, and my steps slow. The labour of winding among the little paths of the mountain and fixing my feet firmly as I advanced perplexed me, occupied as I was by the emotions which the occurrences of the day had produced.

Night was far advanced when I came to the halfway resting-place and seated myself beside the fountain. The stars shone at intervals as the clouds passed from over them; the dark pines rose before me, and every here and there a broken tree lay on the ground; it was a scene of wonderful solemnity and stirred strange thoughts within me. I wept bitterly, and clasping my hands in agony, I exclaimed, “Oh! stars and clouds and winds, ye are all about to mock me; if ye really pity me, crush sensation and memory; let me become as nought; but if not, depart, depart, and leave me in darkness.”

These were wild and miserable thoughts, but I cannot describe to you how the eternal twinkling of the stars weighed upon me and how I listened to every blast of wind as if it were a dull ugly siroc on its way to consume me.

Morning dawned before I arrived at the village of Chamounix; I took no rest, but returned immediately to Geneva. Even in my own heart I could give no expression to my sensations—they weighed on me with a mountain’s weight and their excess destroyed my agony beneath them. Thus I returned home, and entering the house, presented myself to the family. My haggard and wild appearance awoke intense alarm, but I answered no question, scarcely did I speak.

I felt as if I were placed under a ban—as if I had no right to claim their sympathies—as if never more might I enjoy companionship with them. Yet even thus I loved them to adoration; and to save them, I resolved to dedicate myself to my most abhorred task. The prospect of such an occupation made every other circumstance of existence pass before me like a dream, and that thought only had to me the reality of life.

The last part of his story had rekindled the anger that had faded while he described his peaceful life near the cottagers, and when he said this I could no longer hold back the rage that was burning inside me. “I do refuse,” I replied, “and no torture will ever force my consent out of me. You may make me the most miserable of men, but you will never make me despicable in my own eyes. “You are wrong,” the fiend replied, “and instead of threatening you, I am willing to reason with you. I am spiteful because I am miserable. Am I not avoided and hated by all mankind? You, my creator, would tear me to pieces and rejoice; remember that, and tell me why I should pity man more than he pities me. You would not call it murder if you could hurl me into one of those crevasses in the ice and destroy my body, the work of your own hands.

Should I respect man when he condemns me? If he lived with me in mutual kindness, then instead of harming him I would shower him with every benefit, weeping with gratitude that he had accepted me. But that is impossible; human senses are barriers that can never be overcome between us. Yet I will not submit like a humble slave. I will take revenge for my injuries; if I cannot inspire love, I will cause fear, and above all I swear undying hatred towards you, my greatest enemy, because you are my creator. Beware; I will work for your ruin and not stop until I have devastated your heart, so that you will curse the hour you were born.”

A devilish rage came over him as he said this; his face twisted into shapes too horrible for human eyes to look at; but soon he calmed down and went on: “I meant to reason with you. This anger is harmful to me, and you do not stop to consider that you are the reason it is so extreme. If any being felt kindness towards me, I would repay it a hundred times over; for the sake of that one creature I would make peace with the whole human race! But now I am indulging in dreams of happiness that can never come true.

What I am asking of you is reasonable and modest; I demand a creature of the other sex, but as hideous as I am; it is a small comfort, but it is all I can receive, and it will satisfy me. It is true that we will be monsters, cut off from the whole world; but for that very reason we will be more devoted to each other. Our lives will not be happy, but they will be harmless and free from the misery I feel now. Oh, my creator, make me happy; let me feel grateful to you for one kindness! Let me see that I can awaken the sympathy of some living thing; do not refuse my request!”

I was moved. I shuddered when I thought of what might happen if I agreed, but I felt that there was some justice in his argument. His story and the feelings he was now expressing showed that he was a creature of delicate feelings, and as his maker, did I not owe him whatever share of happiness I had the power to give? He saw that my feelings had changed and continued:

“If you agree, neither you nor any other human being will ever see us again; I will go to the vast wilderness of South America. My food is not the same as man’s; I do not kill lambs and young goats to satisfy my hunger; acorns and berries give me enough nourishment. My companion will have the same nature as me and will be content with the same simple food. We will make our bed of dry leaves; the sun will shine on us as it shines on men, and it will ripen our food. The picture I am showing you is peaceful and humane, and you must feel that you could only refuse it out of a reckless love of power and cruelty. Merciless as you have been towards me, I now see compassion in your eyes; let me seize this favourable moment and persuade you to promise what I so passionately desire.”

“You are proposing,” I replied, “to flee from the homes of men and to live in those wild places where the animals of the field will be your only companions. How can you, who long for the love and sympathy of human beings, endure this exile? You will come back and seek their kindness again, and you will meet with their loathing; your evil passions will be revived, and then you will have a companion to help you in your work of destruction. This cannot be; stop arguing, because I cannot agree.”

“How changeable your feelings are! Only a moment ago you were moved by what I said, so why do you harden your heart against my complaints again? I swear to you, by the earth I live on and by you who made me, that with the companion you give me I will leave the places where men live and settle, wherever chance takes me, in the wildest of places. My evil passions will be gone, because I will find sympathy! My life will slip quietly away, and when I am dying I will not curse my maker.”

His words had a strange effect on me. I felt compassion for him and sometimes wished to comfort him, but when I looked at him, when I saw the filthy mass that moved and spoke, my heart turned sick and my feelings changed to horror and hatred. I tried to suppress these feelings; I thought that, since I could not feel sympathy for him, I had no right to deny him the small share of happiness that I still had the power to give.

“You swear,” I said, “to be harmless; but haven’t you already shown so much malice that I have good reason to distrust you? Might this not be a trick to increase your triumph by giving you greater scope for revenge?” “What is this? I will not be played with, and I demand an answer. If I have no bonds and no one to love, hatred and vice must be my lot; the love of another will remove the cause of my crimes, and I will become a being whose existence no one will even know about. My vices are the children of a forced loneliness that I detest, and my virtues will naturally appear when I live in close companionship with an equal. I will feel the affections of a sensitive being and become part of the chain of existence and events from which I am now shut out.”

I paused for some time to think over everything he had told me and all the arguments he had used. I thought of the promise of goodness he had shown at the beginning of his life, and of how every kind feeling had later been blighted by the disgust and contempt his protectors had shown him. I did not leave his power and threats out of my calculations; a creature who could live in the ice caves of the glaciers and escape pursuit among the ridges of unreachable cliffs had abilities that it would be useless to fight against. After thinking for a long time, I concluded that the justice I owed both to him and to my fellow human beings required me to grant his request. So I turned to him and said:

“I agree to your demand, on condition that you solemnly swear to leave Europe for ever, and every other place near human beings, as soon as I hand over to you a female who will go with you into exile.” “I swear,” he cried, “by the sun, and by the blue sky of heaven, and by the fire of love that burns in my heart, that if you grant my prayer, you will never see me again as long as they exist. Go home and begin your work; I will watch its progress with indescribable anxiety; and do not doubt that when you are ready, I will appear.” With these words he suddenly left me, afraid, perhaps, that I might change my mind. I watched him rush down the mountain faster than an eagle flies, and he was soon lost among the waves of the sea of ice.

His story had taken up the whole day, and the sun was on the edge of the horizon when he left. I knew that I ought to hurry down towards the valley, as I would soon be surrounded by darkness; but my heart was heavy, and my steps were slow. The effort of winding along the little mountain paths and placing my feet firmly as I went confused me, absorbed as I was in the emotions that the day’s events had stirred up.

The night was well advanced when I reached the halfway resting place and sat down beside the spring. The stars shone now and then as the clouds drifted away from them; the dark pines rose up in front of me, and here and there a broken tree lay on the ground; it was a scene of wonderful solemnity, and it stirred strange thoughts in me. I wept bitterly and, clasping my hands in agony, cried out, “Oh, stars and clouds and winds, you are all about to mock me; if you truly pity me, crush my feelings and my memory; let me become nothing; but if not, go away, go away, and leave me in darkness.” These were wild and wretched thoughts, but I cannot describe to you how the endless twinkling of the stars weighed on me, and how I listened to every gust of wind as if it were a dull, ugly sirocco coming to devour me.

Dawn broke before I reached the village of Chamounix; I did not rest, but went straight back to Geneva. Even to myself I could not put my feelings into words; they pressed on me with the weight of a mountain, and their very excess crushed my anguish beneath them. So I returned home, went into the house and showed myself to my family. My haggard, wild appearance caused great alarm, but I answered none of their questions and hardly spoke at all.

I felt as if I had been placed under a curse, as if I had no right to their sympathy, as if I could never again enjoy their company. Yet even so I adored them; and to save them, I made up my mind to devote myself to the task I hated most. The thought of such work made everything else in life drift past me like a dream, and only that thought seemed real to me.

This anger is bad for me, and you do not understand that you are the reason for it. If anyone were kind to me, I would be a hundred times kinder in return; for that one creature, I would make peace with all people! But I am dreaming of a happiness that I can never have.

What I am asking for is fair and small. I want a female creature, as ugly as I am. It is not much, but it is all I can have, and it will be enough for me. It is true that we will be monsters and we will live away from the world, but because of that we will love each other more. Our lives will not be happy, but we will not hurt anyone, and we will not suffer as I suffer now. Oh, my creator, make me happy; let me thank you for one good thing! Let me see that some living thing feels for me; please do not say no!”

His words touched me. I was afraid when I thought about what could happen if I agreed, but I felt that he was partly right. His story and his words showed that he had real, deep feelings. I had made him, so did I not have a duty to give him as much happiness as I could? He saw that my feelings had changed, and he continued:

“If you agree, you and other people will never see us again; I will go to the wild lands of South America. I do not eat what people eat; I do not kill young animals for food. Nuts and berries are enough for me. My companion will be like me and will be happy with the same food. We will sleep on dry leaves, and the sun will shine on us just as it shines on people and will make our food grow. The life I am describing is peaceful and gentle, and you must feel that you could only refuse it if you were cruel and loved your power. You have been hard on me, but now I see pity in your eyes; let me use this good moment and ask you to promise what I want so much.”

“You want,” I answered, “to run away from people and live in wild places where your only friends will be animals. But you want people to love you and understand you, so how can you live so far away from them? You will come back and look for their kindness again, and they will hate you again. Your anger will return, and then you will have a partner to help you destroy. This cannot happen; stop arguing, because I cannot agree.”

“How quickly your feelings change! A moment ago my words touched you, so why are you hard and cold to me again? I promise you, by the earth I live on and by you who made me, that if you give me a companion, I will leave the places where people live and go to the wildest places I can find. My evil feelings will go away, because someone will understand me! My life will pass quietly, and when I die, I will not curse the one who made me.”

His words had a strange effect on me. I felt sorry for him, and sometimes I wanted to comfort him. But when I looked at him, at that dirty, ugly thing that moved and talked, I felt sick, and my feelings turned to horror and hate. I tried to fight these feelings. I thought that even if I could not like him, I had no right to keep from him the little happiness that I could still give him.

“You promise,” I said, “not to hurt anyone; but you have already shown how cruel you can be, so why should I trust you? Perhaps this is only a trick to give you more power for your revenge?” “What? Do not play games with me; I want an answer. If I have no friends and no one to love, then hate and evil will be all I have. The love of another creature will take away the reason for my crimes, and nobody will even know that I exist. I do bad things because I am forced to be alone, and I hate being alone; I will be good when I live with someone like me. I will have the feelings of a normal living being, and I will be part of the world, which I am shut out of now.”

I stopped for some time to think about his story and his arguments. I thought about how good he had been at the start of his life, and how people’s hate and disgust had destroyed all his kind feelings. I also thought about his strength and his threats. He could live in ice caves and hide on cliffs where no one could follow him, so it would be useless to fight him. After a long time I decided that, to be fair to him and to other people, I had to do what he asked. So I turned to him and said:

“I agree, but you must promise to leave Europe for ever, and every other place where people live, as soon as I give you a female who will go away with you.” “I swear,” he cried, “by the sun, by the blue sky, and by the love that burns in my heart, that if you do this, you will never see me again while they exist. Go home and start your work. I will watch how it goes, and I will be very anxious. Don’t worry: when you are ready, I will come.” After these words he left me suddenly, perhaps because he was afraid I would change my mind. I saw him go down the mountain faster than an eagle can fly, and soon I lost him among the waves of ice.

His story had taken the whole day, and the sun was going down when he left. I knew that I should hurry down to the valley, because it would soon be dark, but my heart was heavy and I walked slowly. It was hard to follow the narrow mountain paths and to put my feet down carefully, because my mind was full of the feelings of that day.

It was late at night when I came to the resting place halfway down, and I sat down by the spring. The stars appeared from time to time when the clouds moved away. Dark pine trees stood in front of me, and here and there a broken tree lay on the ground. It was a very serious and beautiful scene, and it gave me strange thoughts. I cried bitterly, held my hands together in pain and shouted, “Oh, stars and clouds and winds, you are all laughing at me! If you really feel sorry for me, take away my feelings and my memory; let me become nothing. If not, go away, go away, and leave me in the dark.” These were wild and unhappy thoughts, but I cannot tell you how heavy the endless shining of the stars felt to me. I listened to every wind as if it were a hot, ugly desert wind that was coming to eat me up.

The morning came before I reached the village of Chamounix. I did not rest but went straight back to Geneva. I could not explain my feelings, even to myself; they were as heavy as a mountain, and there were so many of them that I could not even feel my pain. So I came home and went in to see my family. I looked so tired and wild that they were very worried, but I did not answer their questions and I hardly spoke.

I felt as if I were cursed, as if I had no right to their kindness, as if I could never enjoy being with them again. But I still loved them more than anything, and to save them, I decided to give myself to the work I hated most. Thinking about this work made everything else in my life seem like a dream, and only this one thought felt real.
